title: Technical Product Manager - Healthcare Market Insights
descriptionText: Huron helps its clients drive growth, enhance performance and sustain leadership in the markets they serve. We help healthcare organizations build innovation capabilities and accelerate key growth initiatives, enabling organizations to own the future, instead of being disrupted by it. Together, we empower clients to create sustainable growth, optimize internal processes and deliver better consumer outcomes. Health systems, hospitals and medical clinics are under immense pressure to improve clinical outcomes and reduce the cost of providing patient care. Investing in new partnerships, clinical services and technology is not enough to create meaningful and substantive change. To succeed long-term, healthcare organizations must empower leaders, clinicians, employees, affiliates and communities to build cultures that foster innovation to achieve the best outcomes for patients. Joining the Huron team means you’ll help our clients evolve and adapt to the rapidly changing healthcare environment and optimize existing business operations, improve clinical outcomes, create a more consumer-centric healthcare experience, and drive physician, patient and employee engagement across the enterprise. Join our team as the expert you are now and create your future. Huron is seeking a Technical Product Manager and Builder to lead the evolution of healthcare analytics and market intelligence solutions that help healthcare organizations make better strategic, operational, network, and growth decisions. This is an empowered product leader and builder role. It combines product strategy, healthcare domain leadership, technical fluency, and end-to-end accountability for outcomes. The successful candidate owns the why and what, shapes the first version of the how through functional prototypes and technical spikes, and partners closely with Product Owners, Product Design, Engineering, Data Science, Architecture, Consulting, and commercial teams to deliver scalable, trusted, data-driven products. The role operates from executive strategy and customer discovery through detailed product specifications, delivery decisions, release readiness, adoption, and continuous improvement. Success is measured by customer and business outcomes, not features shipped or tickets completed. What You Will Own Product Strategy, Roadmap, and Economics Define and communicate the product vision, strategy, positioning, and evidence-based roadmap for Healthcare Market Insights and related data and analytics capabilities. Prioritize investments by balancing customer value, measurable business impact, competitive differentiation, technical feasibility, scalability, platform coherence, and long-term sustainability. Make and defend lifecycle decisions on when to invest, maintain, partner, buy, or retire; contribute to pricing, packaging, and business-model decisions with commercial and finance partners. Maintain a living view of healthcare trends, regulations, competitors, data sources, and emerging technologies, translating signals into clear product decisions. Continuous Discovery and Product Building Lead continuous discovery with clients, users, consultants, Sales, and Customer Success to distinguish customer requests from underlying problems and validate the outcomes that matter. Partner with Product Design as a co-investigator through interviews, advisory groups, usability studies, beta cohorts, workflow observation, and quantitative product evidence. Build functional prototypes, AI-assisted demos, technical spikes, and proofs of concept using AI tooling, low-code environments, data exploration, or direct API integration to test desirability and feasibility before committing engineering capacity. Synthesize customer, market, usage, and performance signals into concise decisions, product specifications, and roadmap changes. Healthcare Market Insights Domain Leadership Act as a product and domain leader for healthcare data, analytics, and market intelligence, with strong understanding of provider and payer ecosystems, healthcare operations, and strategic planning workflows. Shape solutions addressing provider performance, referral patterns, network integrity, market share, care migration, service-line growth, demand forecasting, and market strategy. Define requirements for healthcare data acquisition, licensing, integration, enrichment, attribution, governance, quality, lineage, transparency, and methodology. Ensure analytic methods and outputs are accurate, traceable, explainable, privacy-conscious, and aligned with applicable industry standards and regulatory expectations. Technical Product and Platform Partnership Partner as a technical peer with Engineering, Data Science, and Architecture on cloud platforms, data pipelines and models, APIs, integrations, interoperability, security, performance, observability, governance, and AI-enabled experiences. Write crisp, build-ready product specifications covering workflows, data requirements, technical constraints, API contracts, edge cases, system behavior, and measurable acceptance criteria. Think beyond individual features to enterprise platform capabilities, reuse, multi-tenancy, extensibility, backward compatibility, developer experience, and maintainability; resist one-off customization that erodes platform coherence. Drive advanced analytics, predictive models, natural-language experiences, intelligent automation, and AI capabilities where they provide validated customer value and can be operated responsibly. Delivery Accountability and Release Outcomes Own the product lifecycle from discovery through adoption and continuous improvement. The Technical Product Manager is accountable for product outcomes and priority; the Product Owner and delivery team are responsible for detailed backlog administration and sprint execution. Provide clear priorities, decision context, epics and features, and outcome-based acceptance measures; collaborate with the Product Owner and Business Analyst on user stories, backlog readiness, release plans, and delivery dependencies. Participate deeply in refinement, architecture discussions, planning, demos, acceptance, incident reviews, and tradeoff decisions without becoming the delivery project manager or engineering manager. Define release-readiness criteria, including quality, privacy, security, performance, error thresholds, data validation, observability, enablement, and support readiness. Own product acceptance, release communication, and post-launch outcome review. Remove or escalate product decision barriers and close the loop after release through adoption, reliability, customer feedback, and business outcome measures. Stakeholder Leadership Serve as the primary product partner across clients, executives, Consulting, Professional Services, Product Design, Engineering, Data Science, Architecture, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance. Communicate strategy, priorities, tradeoffs, roadmap progress, technical implications, and release outcomes with clarity for both technical and non-technical audiences. Build trusted partnerships across globally distributed teams, including U.S. and India-based colleagues, with shared context, effective asynchronous practices, and direct decision-making. Measures of Success Validated customer problems are solved and client workflows improve. Adoption, engagement, retention, and measurable client and business value increase. Roadmap commitments are evidence-based, feasible, and delivered with clear readiness and quality standards. Data, analytics, and AI outputs are trusted, explainable, reliable, and scalable. Engineering and stakeholders receive timely decisions, clear specifications, and fewer avoidable handoffs or rework. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in one of the following: Computer Science, Product Management, Engineering, Data Science, Business, Healthcare Informatics, or relevant field. 7+ years of product management, technical product management, product engineering, healthcare analytics, or related technical leadership experience delivering enterprise software, data, analytics, or platform products. Demonstrated healthcare domain expertise across provider or payer environments, healthcare operations, clinical and financial workflows, healthcare data, privacy, and regulatory considerations. Technical fluency sufficient to interpret system diagrams, data flows, APIs, and code-level tradeoffs and to participate substantively in architecture and engineering discussions. Experience writing technical product specifications, data requirements, edge cases, API or integration requirements, and measurable acceptance criteria. Hands-on experience using AI tools, LLM APIs, agent frameworks, low-code tools, analytics environments, or equivalent methods to prototype and validate product ideas. Proven ability to lead continuous customer discovery, manage roadmaps and backlogs, influence across a matrixed organization, and own outcomes from concept through post-launch performance. Preferred Qualifications Experience with healthcare market intelligence, claims analytics, population health, provider performance, network strategy, or growth strategy solutions. Experience with deidentified healthcare claims, CMS data, X12 transactions, HL7/FHIR, interoperability, healthcare data platforms, and data licensing or governance. Working knowledge of SQL, analytics and visualization platforms, cloud-native and modern data architectures, multi-tenant SaaS, event-driven systems, API design, and observability tooling. Experience delivering AI-enabled products, predictive analytics, natural-language query, intelligent automation, or responsible AI capabilities. Experience with globally distributed engineering teams and asynchronous delivery practices; background in software engineering or data engineering is beneficial. Experience contributing to pricing, packaging, and commercial strategy. Product or Agile certifications such as CSPO, A-CSPO, SAFe POPM, or PMI-ACP are a plus. What Great Looks Like You combine healthcare judgment, customer empathy, business acumen, and technical credibility. You move from insight to a tangible experiment quickly, use prototypes and evidence to reduce risk, and give engineers something clear and real to productionize. You engage deeply enough to understand tradeoffs, but remain focused on product decisions and outcomes. You earn trust by making sound calls, explaining the rationale, and holding the product to a simple standard: does it solve the right problem, does it work reliably, and does it create measurable value? Why Join Huron? Shape strategic healthcare analytics products that help health systems make better growth, network, and market decisions. Work with large-scale healthcare data assets and turn complex information into trusted, decision-ready intelligence. Help define how AI, analytics, and market intelligence improve healthcare decision-making and performance. Join a collaborative culture that values impact, curiosity, integrity, inclusion, excellence, and humility. The estimated base salary for this job is $150,000 - $200,000. The actual salary paid to an individual will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to specific skills or certifications, years of experience, market changes, and required travel. This job is also eligible to participate in Huron’s annual incentive compensation program, which reflects Huron’s pay for performance philosophy. Inclusive of annual incentive compensation opportunity, the total estimated compensation range for this job is $180,000 - $240,000. The job is also eligible to participate in Huron’s benefit plans which include medical, dental and vision coverage and other wellness programs. #LI-REMOTE #LI-CL1 Position Level Senior Manager Country United States of America

title: Principal Engineer
descriptionText: Position Summary We are looking for an experienced Lead Engineer responsible for new product development to join our R&D Engineering team. This role is responsible for leading the development of innovative new products from concept creation through production launch, with a strong focus on mechanical/structural design, engineering analysis, and product realization. This is a key technical leadership role for an engineer with deep expertise in mechanical and structural design; strength and theoretical analysis, with a strong understanding of manufacturing processes, DFM/DFA, and applicable power tool standards. Experience in developing power tools for cable cutting, wire stripping or crimping, is highly desirable. The successful candidate should also demonstrate strong English communication skills, the ability to collaborate effectively in cross-functional and global environments, and strong innovation capabilities to drive product design optimization and technical breakthroughs based on customer needs, technology trends, and application scenarios. Extensive experience in the development of handheld power tools for hydraulic, cable cutting, wire stripping, crimping, and pipe processing applications is required. Key Responsibilities Product Development & Management Lead new product development from concept generation through design, validation, and production launch. Identify technical risks proactively, lead problem-solving efforts, and drive effective corrective actions throughout the development cycle. Lead design reviews, prototype builds, and engineering validation activities. Mechanical Design & Engineering Own the mechanical and structural design of products and subsystems. Perform and guide strength calculations, structural analysis, tolerance analysis, and theoretical engineering evaluations to ensure robust and reliable designs. Lead engineering team to complete concepts, 3D models, detailed drawings, specifications, and technical documentation. Transfer product requirements into practical, manufacturable solutions that balance performance, cost, quality, and user needs. Manufacturing & Cross-Functional Collaboration Apply DFM/DFA principles to improve manufacturability, production efficiency, and cost competitiveness. Partner closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, Product Management, and Test Engineering teams to support successful product launch. Support value engineering and cost optimization initiatives and contribute to platform-based product development. Technical Leadership Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers across the R&D organization. Stay current on industry trends, materials, manufacturing technologies, and competitive products relevant to power tools and cable-processing applications. Qualifications Education & Experience Bachelor’s degree or above in Mechanical Engineering, Product Design Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. 8+ years of experience in new product development related to hydraulic tools and pipe wrenches. Proven experience in mechanical/structural design, engineering analysis, and product commercialization. Demonstrated success delivering projects against quality, schedule, and profitability targets. Technical Skills Strong foundation in structural design, mechanical design, and engineering fundamentals. Solid experience in strength analysis, mechanical calculations, and theoretical analysis. Proficiency in 3D and 2D CAD tools and engineering drawing standards. Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes such as machining, stamping, casting, and assembly. Good understanding of DFM/DFA and production feasibility considerations. Familiarity with relevant power tool standards, product safety requirements, and industry compliance expectations. Professional Skills Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Effective communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across functions. Fluent written and spoken English, with the ability to collaborate effectively in a global environment. Preferred Qualifications Direct experience in the development of products or applications involving hydraulic tools, cable cutting, wire stripping, crimping, and pipe processing tools is highly preferred. Proven experience working effectively with global teams, suppliers, and manufacturing facilities across cross-functional and international environments. descriptionText: About Us: Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others. At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters. This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place. We're seeking a Senior Manager to lead the teams responsible for Learning, Content, and Quality within our Shared Services organization. descriptionText: Role Overview We are seeking a Utility Fire Liaison to support LADWP’s Climate Resilience team in protecting first responders and utility crews working around energized and pressurized water and power infrastructure during wildfires and other emergencies. This role serves as a key link between the utility, first responders, and internal field teams to support safe, coordinated emergency response and post-incident recovery. Reporting within Emergency Management, the Utility Fire Liaison leads training and preparedness efforts focused on fire response, responder safety, Incident Command System integration, and all-hazards readiness. This role is ideal for recently retired fire service officers seeking a second career to contribute to the resilience of their community. This is an opportunity to help create and shape a critical emergency management function at one of the nation’s oldest and largest utilities. This is a contract position with an opportunity to apply for the permanent role. This position will require 3 days per week onsite to local LA office. What You’ll Do Train and support first responders (fire, law enforcement, emergency medical services) on safely operating around utility infrastructure, including energized electrical systems, substations, transmission and distribution assets, dams, reservoirs, pipelines, and other critical facilities. Train utility field crews and supervisors on working within the Incident Command System, including responder roles, unified command and communications protocols. Serve as a liaison, providing subject‑matter expertise on utility infrastructure to incident commanders, emergency operations centers (EOCs), and cooperating agencies during wildfire response and recovery operations. Support wildfire response and recovery efforts, including pre‑incident planning, situational awareness, safety briefings, post‑incident reviews, and lessons‑learned integration into procedures and training. Ignition investigation and compliance, working with the power system and fire agencies to investigate and report on all fire incidents, including causes and recommendations for prevention. Collaborate with Compliance Division to ensure all reporting requirements relating to fire are meeting all regulations. Support Department Emergency Operations Center activations with shift‑based overtime or on‑call work, including nights, weekends, holidays and extended hours. This position's work mode is in-person. What You’ll Bring Certifications or training such as ICS 200/300/400, fire service training, emergency management credentials, or utility safety programs are strongly preferred. Experience in fire service, emergency management, or utility operations, with direct involvement in wildfire response, incident management, or hazardous infrastructure environments. Demonstrated ability to train and engage diverse audiences, such as first responders, line crews, supervisors, and cross‑functional utility teams. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex infrastructure and safety concepts into clear, actionable guidance. Understanding of electric and/or water utility infrastructure and the risks these assets present during fires, emergencies, and extreme heat conditions. Experience coordinating with external agencies, including fire departments, emergency management organizations, and mutual aid partners. Ability to operate effectively during high‑stress, rapidly evolving incidents, balancing safety, operational priorities, and clear communication. You’ll find our engaging, high-performance culture personally fulfilling, professionally challenging, and financially rewarding. We’re committed to diversity and equitable access to employment opportunities based on ability. Your unique contributions and talents will be valued and respected here. When you join our team, you’re helping us make the future friendly.

Applied AI is a small, fast-moving team building a fresh take on how patient care should happen, from intake through ongoing care companionship. While much of the team is focused on research and rapid experimentation, this role is the productionization counterpart — the person who takes what's working and makes it robust, scalable, and reliable enough to run in production at the core of the patient experience. You'll be the key architect of the patient-facing experience end-to-end, owning how the services across the stack fit together. This is a hands-on role for someone who thinks about robustness, scalability, and debuggability from day one, and who can balance building for today with architecting for where the product needs to go over the next several years. Key Responsibilities - Own Service Architecture Own the overall architecture for the Applied AI stack — how individual services blend together into a coherent, end-to-end patient-facing experience, from intake through ongoing companion interactions. - Productionize AI-Driven Experiences Partner with research-focused teammates who move fast on experimentation, and take their work to production: hardening services for uptime, reliability, and scale. Bring engineering rigor to a team that's optimized for speed of iteration. - Reliability & Operational Excellence Instill best practices around debugging, observability, and operational readiness. Design for robustness and scalability from day one rather than retrofitting it later. - Mentorship & Talent Growth Mentor senior technical leaders, elevating engineering capabilities across the organization. Champion initiatives that foster talent density, engineering rigor, and a culture of continuous learning - Ambiguity Navigation & Execution Acceleration Lead through complexity and ambiguity, clarifying direction where ownership is unclear. Remove organizational blockers, simplify decision-making, and accelerate delivery of strategic initiatives - Customer-Centric Engineering Translate customer needs and product goals into scalable technical solutions. Define principles and patterns that embed customer obsession into our platform’s architecture - Sustainability & Scalability Design systems and team boundaries to support sustainable growth. Drive investment in non-functional priorities (e.g., observability, migrations, reliability) early in the design process What You Bring - 15+ years of professional software engineering experience with deep architectural expertise and a record of delivering production systems at scale. - Proven track record of influencing technical strategy and delivering cross-org technical initiatives at the group or organizational level. - Excellent track record standing up services at scale in production, with a demonstrated ability to think about robustness, scalability, and debuggability from day one. - Deep experience owning service architecture across a full stack — understanding how services should blend together, not just how to build any one of them well. - A "productionization" mindset: comfortable being the counterweight to a fast-moving research/experimentation culture, focused on uptime and reliability. - Hands-on engineering ability; you want to stay close to the code and the architecture, not just the roadmap. - Some exposure to LLM/AI services — you don't need deep AI expertise, but you should have tested the waters with LLM or AI-powered systems in some capacity. - Ability to think long-term and build for the future, balancing near-term delivery with durable architecture. - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to partner across research, product, and clinical stakeholders. You'll Thrive Here If You: - Create alignment and momentum in ambiguous or complex technical spaces. - Balance short-term deliverables with long-term scalability, system health, and customer experience. - Lead with curiosity, adaptability, and principled decision-making. - Take initiative to address cross-squad blockers, scale constraints, or misaligned priorities before they escalate. - Drive consistent, action-oriented execution even without perfect clarity. - Mentor senior engineering talent and reinforce a culture of growth, feedback, and high technical standards. - Inspire confidence through transparency, humility, and deep technical credibility. - Advocate for customers through scalable, resilient backend design that anticipates clinical complexity and future scale. - Want to help architect how AI reshapes a company's stack and product, from the inside, from day one. title: Staff Software Engineer
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Xometry is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our Core Platform team. This role is a strategic technical leadership position focused on the architectural evolution of our flagship enterprise partnership. While our current plug-ins function as external add-ons, you will be responsible for re-architecting Xometry’s core application services to live natively within our partner's digital ecosystem. You will shape the technical direction of multiple products, establishing the engineering patterns that allow Xometry’s AI—trained on millions of parts—to operate directly on our partner's native 3D geometry. Your goal is to move the architectural framework toward a "target state" where users experience zero-latency DFM feedback and one-click procurement without ever leaving their primary enterprise design environment. This role requires a hybrid schedule (3 days a week) at our North Bethesda, MD or Waltham, MA office location. How You'll Contribute Software Development and Technical Craft: You will design high-performance solutions that extend beyond a single org, establishing the organizational standards for how Xometry-AI is embedded into external PLM environments. You will advance our architectural framework to ensure it is extensible, scalable, and adheres to strict enterprise SLIs/SLOs. AI Fluency: You will lead the effort to integrate production ML pipelines into the application layer, ensuring the "science fiction speed" promised in our vision is realized through optimized model serving and real-time geometry analysis. In addition, you’ll champion AI-assisted development practices across the team, actively mentoring engineers on effective use of AI tools to accelerate delivery, improve code quality, and reduce toil. Problem Solving and Decision Making: You will solve significant and unique challenges regarding data gravity and security. You'll create formal networks between our partner's and Xometry’s engineering groups to develop new ways of conducting operations—specifically regarding "ring-fenced" data governance where part files remain securely within the partner's network infrastructure. Scope and Impact: You are responsible for establishing the strategic direction and leading the execution of this core integration. You will be a technical and business role model, ensuring that the integration of DFM (Manufacturability) and IQE (Pricing) AI engines creates a distinct, defensible edge for the partnership. Collaboration and Communication: You will facilitate technical discourse across the entire Xometry organization, leading to durable, well-documented decisions. As a primary point of contact for senior leadership, you will guide risk/reward conversations and champion cross-functional development across our marketplace and data science teams. Operational Excellence: You will define the reliability and security standards for our enterprise-grade deployments, whether partner-hosted or Xometry-hosted, ensuring seamless multi-tenant management. What You'll Bring to Xometry Experience: 12+ years of professional software development experience, with a history of scaling complex platforms. Deep Technical Expertise: Expert-level mastery of Python, AWS infrastructure, and modern frontend frameworks (React/NextJS) used for complex enterprise applications. Systems Architect: Proven experience shaping the technical direction of multiple teams and establishing engineering patterns as organizational standards. Strategic Roadmap Execution: A track record of securing endorsement for 6-12 month initiatives and driving them to successful production deployment. Communication Excellence: The ability to influence senior leadership and external partners on technical strategy and long-term technology investments. Education: Bachelor’s in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience. You Would Be A Great Fit With Platform Experience: Background in building "Software as a Service" (SaaS) platforms or complex B2B integration hubs. Industrial Tech Background: Experience with manufacturing, logistics, or CAD/PLM software ecosystems. Security & Governance: Deep understanding of enterprise data controls, dedicated tenants, and SOC2/ISO compliance within a cloud environment. Distributed Systems: Experience architecting large-scale ML platforms or high-frequency marketplace engines. Compensation & Benefits The estimated base salary range for new hires into this role is $170,000 – $195,000 annually + annual bonus, depending on factors such as job-related skills, relevant experience, and location. The total compensation package includes base, bonus, and equity. We also offer a competitive benefits package, including: 401(k) match Medical, dental, and vision insurance Life and disability insurance Generous paid time off including vacation, sick leave, floating and fixed holidays Maternity and bonding leave Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and other wellbeing resources A stipend for catered lunch on Tuesdays and Thursdays Xometry is an

descriptionText: At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.Team DescriptionThe Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers. Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact.About the Team This team owns the infrastructure layer between applications and foundation models: model access, routing, reliability, security integration, observability, and cost management behind a single governed interface. Product teams build on the platform instead of integrating with model providers directly, which means the enterprise adopts new model capability once, centrally, rather than many times over. Sitting in the request path for every AI-powered application makes latency, reliability, and efficiency company-level outcomes rather than local ones.This team also owns a measurement and attribution layer that makes consumption legible to the optimization capabilities that act on it, including intelligent routing, caching, context optimization, and capacity planning. The objective is cost per unit of business outcome, not spend reduction in isolation. The architecture set now will determine the enterprise's cost curve and build velocity for years, and this role owns both those decisions and the teams that execute them.In this role, you will: Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital OneOversee the design, development, testing, deployment, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.Make high judgment build-vs-buy decisions across a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, Nemo Guardrails, PyTorch, and moreInvent and introduce state-of-the-art LLM optimization techniques to improve the performance — scalability, cost, latency, throughput — of large scale production AI systemsContribute to the technical vision and the long term roadmap of foundational AI systems at Capital OneAttract and retain top talent in the AI industry and nurture personal and professional development for your team. Foster a culture of learning and staying abreast of the state-of-the-art in AIThe Ideal Candidate:You love to build systems, take pride in the quality of your work, and also share our passion to do the right thing. You want to work on problems that will help change banking for goodPassion for staying abreast of the latest research, and an ability to intuitively understand scientific publications and judiciously apply novel techniques in productionYou get fulfillment from empowering others to achieve their potential and you actively drive professional development through mentoring and coaching. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. TailorCare is a remote-first company with our corporate office located in Nashville. About the Role TailorCare is investing in the people and systems needed to scale our contact center operations efficiently. As our Senior Workforce Management Analyst, you will manage forecasting, scheduling, and real-time adherence across our care teams, ensuring we have the right people in the right place at the right time to deliver an exceptional patient experience. This role is both analytical and operational: you’ll build and maintain staffing models, coordinate closely with our contact center teams to serve as the contact center’s primary resource for capacity planning and workforce tooling, as well as working with our Marketing team to ensure calling campaigns appropriately align with workforce schedules. As TailorCare scales and brings a new CCaaS platform online, you’ll contribute to how WFM practices are built into our systems and workflows. Primary Responsibilities Forecasting & Capacity Planning Own short- and long-term volume forecasting for inbound and outbound contact center activity across all care teams (Care Associates, Care Coordinators, Clinical Navigators). Build and maintain staffing models that account for service level targets, handle times, shrinkage, and growth projections. Partner with care team managers to develop shift plans, PTO strategies, and contingency coverage models. Produce capacity planning analyses to support headcount decisions and hiring timelines. Monitor real-time adherence and queue performance, identifying and escalating deviations from plan and activating coverage adjustments as needed. Maintain and update scheduling tools and WFM platform configurations as team structures, hours, or workflows change. Facilitate daily or weekly operational stand-ups with care team managers to align on coverage, flag risks, and coordinate same-day adjustments. Outbound Campaign Coordination Partner with Marketing and care teams to plan, schedule, and execute outbound calling campaigns, including capacity allocation, timing, and dialer configuration. Translate campaign goals (volume targets, contact windows, member segments) into agent scheduling and workload plans. Hands-on experience with WFM/WEM platforms (e.g., Five9 WFM, NICE WFM, Genesys WFM, or similar). Hands-on experience with CRM and telephony/CCaaS systems; experience with outbound dialer platforms a plus. Strong quantitative and analytical skills; able to build and maintain staffing and forecasting models. Experience coordinating outbound campaign scheduling or working closely with outbound operations teams. Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills; able to manage schedules and configurations for a multi-team environment independently. Comfortable building and documenting WFM processes in a growing function. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to partner cross-functionally across clinical, operational, and marketing teams. Ability and willingness to travel up to 10% as needed for onsite meetings, team collaboration, and company events. Nice to Have Experience implementing or configuring WFM tools as part of a CCaaS migration or new platform deployment. Experience in healthcare, care navigation, or another highly-regulated environment. Exposure to real-time operations monitoring and SLA management in a high-volume contact center. title: Salesforce Solutions Architect
descriptionText: Hometown empowers schools with seamless digital tools for ticketing, fundraising, and event management, enabling them to create memorable in-person experiences that bring communities together. As a trusted partner dedicated to supporting athletics, arts, and extracurricular activities, we help schools generate vital funding to ensure every student has access to enriching opportunities. With a deep passion for serving those who shape our future, we make event operations effortless – so schools can focus on what truly matters: creating lasting impact in their hometowns. Job Description: Location: Remote Type: Full-time, independent contractor (long-term engagement) Hours: Full-time, with a minimum of 5 hours of daily overlap with US Eastern Time (9:00am–5:00pm ET core business hours) Who We Are: Hometown is the trusted leader in the education space, equipping athletic directors, coaches, and school administrators with the tools they need to manage their department communications, live events, and fundraisers. Hometown offers an all-in-one, easy-to-use platform to support schools in creating memorable in-person experiences and lasting impact in their communities. We’re continuing to expand our technology and team to provide the best-in-class service to organizations across the country! Hometown empowers all team members through a positive company culture. Exemplifying our core values of Hustle, Excellence, Resilience, and Ownership (HERO). We’re committed to providing a safe and inclusive work experience for everyone, both those working remotely and within our offices across the country. Consider joining our team today! Role Summary: We are looking for a Salesforce Solutions Architect to own our Salesforce instance end to end. You will be the technical owner of the platform that runs our go-to-market motion. You will be a part of our Business Operations team and report directly to our Senior Director of Operations. This is a hands-on ownership role, not an advisory one. You will inherit a mature, actively used org with automations, integrations, and reporting dependencies, and you will be responsible for keeping it healthy, making it better, and expanding it to support our multi-product go-to-market strategy across ticketing, fundraising, and websites and mobile apps. The person who succeeds here is someone who has done this at more than one company, can reverse-engineer an unfamiliar org, can receive business requirements directly from Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Finance, and can then design, build, test, and ship the change themselves. We are hiring for judgment and ownership as much as for build skill. You will be the person the business asks “can Salesforce do this?” and the person who decides the answer and implements it. Key Responsibilities: Ownership of the Salesforce instance: declarative configuration, permission sets and profiles, page layouts, record types, sharing rules, sandbox strategy, and release management. Maintain and stabilize: inherit the existing automation footprint (Flows, validation rules, assignment logic, approval processes), document what exists, retire what’s redundant, and eliminate the technical debt that accumulates in any fast-moving org. Improve and expand: identify friction in how our reps and CS team actually work, propose the fix, and ship it. Reduce clicks, improve data quality, and make the system reflect how the business actually sells. Build out our multi-product GTM in Salesforce: design the data model, opportunity architecture, product catalog, and pipeline structure required to sell, renew, and report on multiple products to the same school and district accounts. This includes cross-sell and upsell motion, product-level revenue reporting, bundling, and renewal architecture. Own the integrated stack: maintain and improve how Salesforce connects to Snowflake (our data warehouse), Gong (conversation intelligence and deal insight), and our other go-to-market and billing systems. Partner on data flows in both directions and ensure Salesforce remains the trusted source of truth for GTM data. Reporting and dashboards: build and maintain the reports, dashboards, and forecasting views that leadership, sales management, and Customer Success run on. Be opinionated about what “good” looks like. Gather requirements autonomously: run your own discovery with stakeholders across Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Finance, and leadership. Translate business problems into system design without requiring a project manager or business analyst in between. Governance and enablement: own user management and onboarding, data hygiene standards, field and object documentation, change control, and training for end users on what you build. Vendor and AppExchange management: evaluate, implement, and rationalize the third-party tools connected to the org. Preferred Education and Experience: 4–8 years of hands-on Salesforce experience, including primary ownership of at least one production org. Experience across multiple companies’ Salesforce instances. You’ve walked into orgs you didn’t build, figured out how they work, and improved them. We need someone who has done the inheriting before. Deep declarative expertise: Flow (record-triggered, screen, scheduled), validation rules, formula fields, dynamic forms, approval processes, permission set and sharing architecture, and complex data modeling. Comfortable reading, debugging, and reasoning about code. You can open Apex, triggers, and Lightning Web Components, understand what they do, identify when they’re the cause of a problem, and work with a developer or vendor to fix them. Reporting and data fluency: advanced Salesforce reporting, data loading and migration Integration experience. You’ve owned or heavily supported Salesforce integrations with a data warehouse, conversation intelligence tooling, marketing automation, or billing systems. Salesforce Administrator certification required; Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder, or Sales Cloud Consultant strongly preferred. Professional English fluency, written and verbal. You’ll be running requirements conversations directly with US-based stakeholders, including leadership. Demonstrated autonomy: a track record of operating as the only Salesforce person in the room, setting your own priorities against business goals, and driving change without being managed task to task. Nice To Have: Experience in B2B SaaS selling to schools, districts, higher education, or the public sector. Sandbox and deployment discipline: change sets, SFDX, Gearset, Copado, or similar. Experience with Salesforce AI features (Agentforce, Einstein) or Salesforce-connected AI tooling. Experience supporting a company through a product expansion, acquisition integration, or org consolidation. Experience architecting multi-product or multi-line-of-business selling in Salesforce (product catalog, CPQ or CPQ-adjacent quoting, bundling, product-level revenue reporting). Compensation: Fixed monthly amount of $5,000 USD Our compensation ranges are determined by a variety of factors, including role responsibilities, market data, and an individual's skills, experience, and qualifications. The final offer will be based on these factors and discussed throughout the interview process. Physical Requirements: Must be able to remain stationary for a long period of time, including working on a computer. This position may also be required to travel to client sites or conferences. This could include standing and walking for prolonged periods of time, and while outdoors in various weather conditions. Hometown values the importance of demonstrating to our customers that we care and are invested in our product and how it can be the best solution for them. All Hometown employees have a minimum amount of client events they must attend per year. This may include traveling to local client sites and could include standing and walking for prolonged periods of time, and while outdoors in various weather conditions.

Join our world-class team as we build and deploy AI solutions that empower physicians and transform patient care—making a meaningful impact on millions of lives. Driven by our mission, we prioritize transparency, inclusion, and close collaboration, bringing together exceptional people to revolutionize healthcare. descriptionText: Position Overview Mainly responsible for multi-body dynamics simulation modeling and load mathematical modeling of mechanical systems. Collaborate with other teams to complete system-level integration, including the development and integration of degradation models and control algorithms for key components such as motors, batteries, and inverters. Main Responsibilities Establish multi-body dynamics simulation models for mechanical systems to support product development and design optimization. Communicate closely with the product team to understand product requirements and develop and refine mathematical models of loads. Be familiar with one-dimensional degradation models of key subsystems such as motors, batteries, and inverters. Integrate various models (multi-body dynamics, load, degradation, etc.) at the system level to achieve collaborative simulation and validation of the overall system. Proficient in using system-level simulation platforms such as Ansys Twin Builder for modeling, and capable of benchmarking, calibrating, and optimizing models against experimental data. Participate in model development, simulation process standardization, and the preparation of related technical documentation. Capable of basic or advanced programming (such as Python, C/C++, etc.) to automate and extend the simulation toolchain. Stay abreast of industry-leading technologies, continuously improve system simulation capabilities, and provide technical support for product innovation. Requirements Master’s degree or above in Mechanical Engineering, Power Engineering, Automation, Vehicle Engineering, or related fields. 8+ years of relevant work experience, with expertise in multi-body dynamics modeling and simulation of mechanical systems, and familiarity with mainstream simulation software (such as Ansys Twin Builder, Simscape, etc.). title: Senior Manager, Clinical Quality and Documentation Integrity
descriptionText: Grow Therapy is on a mission to serve as the trusted partner for therapists growing their practice, and patients accessing high-quality care. Powered by technology, we are a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Following the mass increase in depression and anxiety, the need for accessibility is more important than ever. To make our vision for mental healthcare a reality, we’re building a team of entrepreneurs and mission-driven go-getters. Since launching in February 2021, we’ve empowered more than ten thousand therapists and hundreds of thousands of clients across the country and insurance landscape. We’ve raised more than $328Mm in funding, including our Series D, at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others. The Opportunity: The Senior Manager, Clinical Quality & Documentation Integrity leads Grow's Clinical Quality branch, owning provider quality outcomes, documentation standards, and payor audit readiness across a network of 26,000+ independently licensed providers. You will manage Clinical Quality Associates, set the clinical standard across workstreams, and operate as a highly independent leader who drives results without requiring close direction. This role is a clinical subject matter expert. You will translate clinical standards into language that non-clinical partners can act on, and you will hold that standard even when you are not the final decision maker. You work cross-functionally with Product, Operations, and Payor Partnerships teams, not to own their work, but to ensure the clinical standard is represented and applied in what Grow builds and executes. What You’ll Be Doing: - Lead and develop a team, setting clear expectations, managing performance directly, and building a team that surfaces problems and drives solutions independently - Own the provider quality and termination process by defining what clinical quality means, setting and maintaining the clinical standard across the provider network, and owning the criteria and documentation process for provider quality review, escalation, and termination decisions. - Own documentation integrity standards and payor audit readiness by defining what clinically complete and defensible documentation looks like, proactively identifying documentation compliance gaps across the network, and ensuring Grow is payor audit-ready - Serve as the clinical subject matter expert for cross-functional partners. You will build initiatives and projects with Clinical Operations and other internal teams, assess clinical soundness, and ensure clinical requirements are accurately represented in product builds, operational workflows, and payor-facing deliverables. - Review cross-functional initiatives for clinical integrity — when Clinical Operations or another team builds a project or initiative, this role owns the clinical review layer: ensuring it is clinically sound, flagging risk, and recommending adjustments before execution. - Identify issues across all branch workstreams, drive toward resolution independently, and surface blockers with a clear recommended path forward You’ll Be a Good Fit If: - You hold an active, unrestricted clinical license (LCSW, LMFT, LPC, PsyD, PhD, or equivalent) - You have 5–7 years of clinical quality experience - You have direct experience managing a clinical quality team (not clinical supervision) and are comfortable addressing performance directly and constructively - You have direct experience with payor audit response, documentation compliance reviews, or clinical documentation standards in a behavioral health context. - You can clearly articulate clinical standards and documentation requirements to non-clinical partners and translate clinical logic into something actionable without losing the rigor. - You are comfortable being the clinical expert in a room where you may not have final decision authority, and you know how to advocate for the clinical standard while maintaining a collaborative, non-blocking relationship with partners. Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is: Fully Remote Commitment: $130,000 - 159,000 USD Annually Hybrid Commitment: $155,000 - $190,000 USD Annually This role can be hybrid (onsite from our NYC, San Francisco, or Seattle hub location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) or fully remote. Both arrangements include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites). The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location. title: Clinical Navigator - PT - PRN
descriptionText: About TailorCare TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By carefully assessing patients' symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose and navigate the most effective treatment pathway for them every step of the way. TailorCare values the experiences and perspectives of individuals from all backgrounds. We are a highly collaborative, curious, and determined team passionate about scaling a high-growth start-up to improve the lives of those in pain. TailorCare is a remote-first company with our corporate office located in Nashville. About the Role The Clinical Navigator is a licensed Doctor of Physical Therapy responsible for delivering high-quality clinical navigation through both telephonic and video-based member interactions in a fast-paced, metrics-driven clinical operations environment. This role serves as the primary point of contact for members throughout their TailorCare journey, engaging members through outbound and inbound calls, virtual visits, and digital touchpoints to assess needs, build trust, drive participation, and support adherence to evidence-based care plans. Success in this role requires a strong balance of clinical expertise, operational excellence, communication skills, and the ability to consistently meet engagement, productivity, quality, and member outcome goals. Clinical Navigators spend the majority of their workday actively engaging with members while leveraging technology, AI-enabled tools, predictive insights, and standardized workflows to personalize care, improve efficiency, and optimize outcomes. The ideal candidate thrives in a high-volume virtual environment, is energized by member engagement, embraces innovation, and demonstrates accountability for both member outcomes and operational performance. As TailorCare continues to evolve its clinical offerings, this role will play a foundational part in expanding virtual musculoskeletal care navigation. Clinical Navigators will help shape and support future virtual physical therapy programs, leveraging their clinical expertise to deliver increasingly comprehensive care experiences through digital and video-enabled platforms. Primary Responsibilities Member Engagement & Clinical Navigation Serve as the primary navigator for an assigned member population, managing members from intake through program completion in a contact center environment. Conduct comprehensive clinical intake assessments to evaluate MSK conditions, functional limitations, treatment history, goals, and readiness for care. Deliver clinical navigation through both telephonic and video-based interactions, selecting the most effective engagement modality to support member needs and outcomes. Maintain a high volume of daily member interactions through outbound and inbound outreach while delivering a personalized, empathetic, and clinically sound experience. Build trust and engagement through motivational interviewing, behavioral coaching, and evidence-based communication techniques. Educate members on treatment options, clinical recommendations, and available resources to support informed decision-making. Proactively follow up with members to drive adherence, address barriers to care, reinforce treatment plans, and improve engagement outcomes. Monitor member progress and identify opportunities for intervention, escalation, or additional support. Act as a trusted advocate throughout the member journey, ensuring continuity of care and a seamless member experience. Support the evolution of TailorCare’s virtual care capabilities by participating in the development, implementation, and future delivery of virtual physical therapy services and digital MSK care programs. Operational Excellence & Performance Consistently achieve established operational performance metrics, including member engagement targets, outreach productivity, call and video visit quality, follow-up completion rates, documentation accuracy, and care plan adherence metrics. Effectively manage daily workflows, outreach queues, and member caseloads while balancing quality and efficiency in a call center-like environment. Demonstrate strong time management, accountability, and discipline within a high-volume call center and virtual care environment. Maintain readiness and availability for scheduled member interactions throughout the workday. Utilize performance dashboards, reporting tools, and operational data to prioritize outreach activities and maximize member engagement. Embrace continuous improvement initiatives and adapt quickly to evolving workflows, processes, technologies, and organizational priorities. Technology, AI & Innovation Leverage AI-powered tools, predictive analytics, automation, and workflow technologies to enhance member interactions and improve operational efficiency. Utilize clinical decision-support tools and data-driven recommendations to personalize engagement strategies and support evidence-based care navigation. Identify opportunities to improve workflows, member experiences, and operational effectiveness through innovative thinking and feedback. Maintain proficiency across multiple technology platforms, communication tools, telehealth systems, CRMs, and documentation systems. Contribute to the adoption and optimization of emerging technologies that support scalable, high-quality clinical navigation and virtual care delivery. Care Coordination & Collaboration Collaborate closely with interdisciplinary care teams, providers, health plan partners, and internal stakeholders to ensure a coordinated and seamless member experience. Communicate timely updates regarding member progress, barriers, escalations, and clinical concerns. Escalate complex clinical or operational issues appropriately while maintaining ownership of the member experience. Partner with colleagues across Clinical Operations, Product, Technology, and Provider Success teams to continuously improve the member journey. Contribute to a collaborative team culture through knowledge sharing, peer support, and participation in team meetings, training initiatives, and workflow improvement efforts. Documentation & Compliance Accurately document all member interactions, assessments, care plans, and outreach efforts within established timelines. Ensure compliance with clinical protocols, quality standards, documentation requirements, and organizational policies. Maintain confidentiality and adhere to all applicable regulatory requirements and professional standards. Other duties as assigne Qualifications Required Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) or Masters in Physical Therapy (MPT) Current unrestricted Physical Therapy license in Georgia, Texas, Colorado and/or Indiana (Compact License preferred). Willingness to obtain and maintain additional state licenses as TailorCare expands. Minimum 3 years of experience in physical therapy, musculoskeletal care, care navigation, telehealth, or related clinical settings. Demonstrated success managing patient interactions in high-volume, performance-oriented environments. Strong communication, motivational interviewing, and patient engagement skills. Experience utilizing technology and data to improve workflow efficiency and patient outcomes. Ability to work independently while maintaining accountability to productivity, engagement, and quality expectations. Comfortable working across multiple technology platforms, communication tools, and dual-monitor environments. Ability and willingness to travel up to 10% as needed for onsite meetings, team collaboration, and company events. Preferred Experience in telephonic care navigation, virtual care, care management, population health, utilization management, or digital health environments. Experience working within a call center, contact center, or metrics-driven healthcare operations setting. Familiarity with AI-enabled clinical tools, workflow automation, and digital health technologies. Experience in value-based care, employer-sponsored healthcare programs, or population health initiatives. Experience in high-growth startup environments. Skills Member Engagement & Relationship Building High-Volume Telephonic & Video-Based Communication Motivational Interviewing & Behavior Change Coaching Clinical Assessment & Care Planning Operational Excellence & Productivity Management Data-Driven Decision Making Virtual Care Delivery & Telehealth Excellence AI & Technology Utilization Adaptability & Continuous Improvement Cross-Functional Collaboration Accountability & Results Orientation What's In It For You Meaningful Work: We are dedicated to our mission and deeply value our patients and each other. Each day offers the opportunity to make a positive impact. Work Environment: We operate as a remote-first company with options for a hybrid work model in Nashville. Time Off: Our generous paid time off (PTO) and holiday plans ensure you have ample time to rest and recharge. Family First: We offer paid parental leave and support a healthy work-life balance, encouraging flexibility and autonomy. We love talking about our family and pets! Comprehensive Benefits: From Day 1, employees enjoy medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, wellness resources and an employer HSA contribution. Fair Compensation: We are committed to equitable pay for all team members and support your future goals with a 401k plan that includes employer matching. As Xometry moves from transactional custom parts into recurring production programs, the planning problem changes shape. This is a build role as much as a run role. title: Staff Product Manager, Financial Systems
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Every dollar that moves through Xometry passes through Financial Systems: what a buyer is quoted and invoiced, what a partner is paid and when, what gets disputed, what gets recognized as revenue, and what finally lands in the ledger. As Staff Product Manager for Financial Systems, you will sit at the intersections of the order-to-cash and procure-to-pay lifecycles. You will collaborate with cross functional product teams making Xometry the most dependable marketplace for partners and customers. This is an individual contributor position that requires product manager proficiency and a deep understanding of financial and accounting operational functions and internal control concepts. You will be expected to read a journal entry, trace a transaction through to the general ledger, and understand why a control exists, or doesn’t, before you create a solution. Day to day, you will gather requirements from customers, partners, and our own Accounting team, and translate what you learn into products & features that serve all three. You will translate finance requirements into PRDs that engineers can design and build from. How You'll Contribute: Identify & Prioritize: Identify, define, and prioritize features & product enhancements that matter. You will communicate the value to the organization, and develop the metrics using data that supports the business case. Know the Personas: Develop a deep understanding of finance, procurement and operational persons and their end to end workflows from both the customer and internal accounting teams perspective so that requirements reflect how the work actually gets done from both the Procure to Pay and Order to Cash lenses. Cross Functional Alignment: Act as the hub between Engineering, Finance and Accounting, Sales, Order Operations, Partner Experience, Legal, and Tax, so that launches land with the field ready and users are informed. Own Release Enablement End to End: For every release, you own the communication, documentation, SOPs, and training, and coordinate with Marketing to inform customers and partners. Ensure that the work done turns a deployed feature into an adopted one. Build Controls into the Product: Partner with Accounting, Controllership, Tax, and Internal Audit so that segregation of duties, approval thresholds, the audit trail, revenue recognition treatment, and SOX-relevant controls are designed into workflows rather than reconciled around them afterward. Collaborate with other product managers to guide them through finance required specifications necessary for feature sign off and acceptance. Apply automation and AI where it is verifiable: Target the highest volume of manual work such as cash application, invoice exception handling, dispute triage, payout inquiries with automation that is measurable, reversible, and gated by human review where the cost of a silent error is high. Deconstruct Complex Problems: Break large, ambiguous problems into smaller pieces that deliver iterative wins, without losing sight of the outcome they add up to. Research & Auditing: You will work with accounts receivable and accounts payable teams and research/troubleshoot complex sales orders, purchase orders, general ledger postings and determine a course of action. What You'll Bring to Xometry: 8+ years of product, program or project management experience, and 4+ years in an accounting related role such as book keeping, staff accounting or audit. Accounting fundamentals are at the core of this position. Working fluency with accounting fundamentals, accrual concepts, revenue recognition, chart of accounts, reconciliation, month end close, audit and SOX controls sufficient to partner with Controllership and Accounting as peers rather than as requesters. Experience working with accounting software platforms (Sage Intacct, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar) that include the general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable or procurement subledgers, and how journal entries are recorded between ledgers; or homegrown systems that act as the subledger. Experience designing policy driven workflows (credit limits, approval routing, tiered sign-off, exception queues, escalation logic) rather than single user tools. Track record integrating with ERP platforms and third party solutions such as Stripe, Avalara, High Radius, Zuora, and eProcurment providers such as Coupa and Ariba. Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to distill financial and operational complexity into a clear narrative for engineers and executives alike. Proven ability to operate autonomously with a passion for problem solving and diving deep into transactional ecosystems to understand the micro details that are recorded in accounting systems. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Every dollar that moves through Xometry passes through Financial Systems: what a buyer is quoted and invoiced, what a partner is paid and when, what gets disputed, what gets recognized as revenue, and what finally lands in the ledger. As Staff Product Manager for Financial Systems, you will sit at the intersections of the order-to-cash and procure-to-pay lifecycles. You will collaborate with cross functional product teams making Xometry the most dependable marketplace for partners and customers. This is an individual contributor position that requires product manager proficiency and a deep understanding of financial and accounting operational functions and internal control concepts. You will be expected to read a journal entry, trace a transaction through to the general ledger, and understand why a control exists, or doesn’t, before you create a solution. Day to day, you will gather requirements from customers, partners, and our own Accounting team, and translate what you learn into products & features that serve all three. You will translate finance requirements into PRDs that engineers can design and build from. How You'll Contribute: Identify & Prioritize: Identify, define, and prioritize features & product enhancements that matter. You will communicate the value to the organization, and develop the metrics using data that supports the business case. Know the Personas: Develop a deep understanding of finance, procurement and operational persons and their end to end workflows from both the customer and internal accounting teams perspective so that requirements reflect how the work actually gets done from both the Procure to Pay and Order to Cash lenses. Cross Functional Alignment: Act as the hub between Engineering, Finance and Accounting, Sales, Order Operations, Partner Experience, Legal, and Tax, so that launches land with the field ready and users are informed. Own Release Enablement End to End: For every release, you own the communication, documentation, SOPs, and training, and coordinate with Marketing to inform customers and partners. Ensure that the work done turns a deployed feature into an adopted one. Build Controls into the Product: Partner with Accounting, Controllership, Tax, and Internal Audit so that segregation of duties, approval thresholds, the audit trail, revenue recognition treatment, and SOX-relevant controls are designed into workflows rather than reconciled around them afterward. Collaborate with other product managers to guide them through finance required specifications necessary for feature sign off and acceptance. Apply automation and AI where it is verifiable: Target the highest volume of manual work such as cash application, invoice exception handling, dispute triage, payout inquiries with automation that is measurable, reversible, and gated by human review where the cost of a silent error is high. Deconstruct Complex Problems: Break large, ambiguous problems into smaller pieces that deliver iterative wins, without losing sight of the outcome they add up to. Research & Auditing: You will work with accounts receivable and accounts payable teams and research/troubleshoot complex sales orders, purchase orders, general ledger postings and determine a course of action. What You'll Bring to Xometry: 8+ years of product, program or project management experience, and 4+ years in an accounting related role such as book keeping, staff accounting or audit. Accounting fundamentals are at the core of this position. Working fluency with accounting fundamentals, accrual concepts, revenue recognition, chart of accounts, reconciliation, month end close, audit and SOX controls sufficient to partner with Controllership and Accounting as peers rather than as requesters. Experience working with accounting software platforms (Sage Intacct, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar) that include the general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable or procurement subledgers, and how journal entries are recorded between ledgers; or homegrown systems that act as the subledger. Experience designing policy driven workflows (credit limits, approval routing, tiered sign-off, exception queues, escalation logic) rather than single user tools. Track record integrating with ERP platforms and third party solutions such as Stripe, Avalara, High Radius, Zuora, and eProcurment providers such as Coupa and Ariba. Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to distill financial and operational complexity into a clear narrative for engineers and executives alike. Proven ability to operate autonomously with a passion for problem solving and diving deep into transactional ecosystems to understand the micro details that are recorded in accounting systems. Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or business, or 10+ years in an accounting related field; advanced degree (MBA,MS, MAcc) and ASC 606 a plus The estimated base salary range for new hires into this role is $180,000–$207,000 annually + bonus, depending on factors such as job-related skills, relevant experience, and location. title: CA Licensed Psychiatrist, Concert Care Psychiatry — Adult ADHD
descriptionText: Who We Are Concert Health is a mission-driven behavioral health medical group delivering evidence-based Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) services in primary care. Our Concert Care Psychiatry program provides essential support for patients with complex adult ADHD diagnostic and short-term treatment needs, enabling primary care providers (PCPs) to confidently manage adult ADHD within the integrated care framework. The program emphasizes focused engagement, clinical stabilization, and a smooth transition of care back to the PCP. Thoughtful diagnosis. Real clinical support. Compensation that never depends on prescribing volume. This role was designed for psychiatrists who want to practice at the top of their license: taking the time to reach the right diagnosis, treating the whole patient rather than the most convenient symptom, and working alongside a team that gives them the context to do it well. What Sets This Role Apart Compensation independent of prescribing. Your pay is never tied to number of scripts, refills, or visit volume. You're supported for practicing sound medicine — including when that means concluding a patient doesn't have ADHD, prioritizing an underlying anxiety disorder first, or holding off on a stimulant until the picture is clearer. A genuine care team, not a caseload. Every patient arrives with groundwork already done by a Behavioral Health Care Manager (BHCM), along with full visibility into the patient's primary care record and a direct line to their PCP. You start each visit with far more clinical context than most consultative psychiatry roles provide. Built around diagnosis, not maintenance. The role centers on the highest-value clinical work — differential diagnosis, treatment planning, and getting patients started on the right path — rather than long-term refill management. If diagnostic work is what you find most rewarding, this position is structured around it. A true integrated care model. This isn't a stand-alone telepsychiatry queue with a fixed visit clock. You're embedded in a coordinated care team — a BHCM handling intake and follow-up, a PCP you can consult directly, and a shared record available before every visit. That structure is what allows for the kind of careful, collaborative practice that a strong diagnosis requires. Rather than competing on volume-based compensation, we're built around sustainable, high-integrity clinical practice. What You'll Do Conduct comprehensive adult ADHD evaluations, including structured interviews, validated rating scales (e.g., ASRS), and rigorous differential diagnosis Prescribe and manage stimulant and non-stimulant medications with full clinical latitude to address comorbid anxiety, mood, or other conditions first when appropriate Partner on an ongoing basis with a BHCM and the patient's PCP, rather than a one-time handoff Deliver short-term, measurement-based consultative care that stabilizes patients and supports a smooth transition back to primary care management Serve as a clinical resource for PCPs managing adult ADHD questions in their own patient panels What We're Looking For Active, unrestricted medical license to practice psychiatry in California Active DEA registration in California MD or DO from an accredited medical school Board certification in Psychiatry (ABPN or AOBNP) 5+ years of post-residency clinical experience, with demonstrated expertise in diagnosing and treating adult ADHD Familiarity with measurement-based care tools and comorbidity screening (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) Experience in integrated or team-based primary care settings is a strong plus A genuine commitment to diagnostic accuracy and patient-centered care What We Offer Flexible, part-time schedule options Base salary range: $270,000–$340,000 (full-time equivalent; pro-rated based on schedule) Fully remote W-2 employment Who Thrives Here Psychiatrists who want to be part of building a differentiated, clinically rigorous integrated care model — including those who have grown frustrated with high-volume telehealth practices and are looking for a more sustainable, team-based way to practice. title: Director of Transportation, Plasma
descriptionText: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. What you do at McKesson matters.
