title: Staff Cloud Security Engineer
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Xometry is looking for a Staff Cloud Security Engineer to own our cloud security posture and runtime detection capabilities. This is a high-impact, individual contributor role focused on ensuring our live cloud environments and containerized workloads are hardened, continuously monitored, and generating the right signals for our security operations function. This role is about detection architecture, posture management, and runtime visibility. You will be the primary owner of our CrowdStrike platform, working closely with our MDR providers to ensure alert fidelity, tuning, and appropriate escalation. You will also evaluate and potentially implement a cloud SIEM. This isn’t a role where you watch dashboards and write tickets. You’ll be the person who defines how we detect threats, decides how we respond to them, and has the autonomy to fix what you find. If you’re tired of maintaining legacy tooling, navigating slow change management processes, or writing findings that disappear into a backlog, this is the opposite of that. We’re a SaaS-first company running a modern, cloud-native stack. We ship fixes, not tickets. What You'll Contribute Own CrowdStrike Falcon configuration, ensuring policies are appropriately scoped, tuned, and generating actionable alerts. Partner with MDR to define alert routing, triage thresholds, and escalation logic, ensuring the right signals reach the right team. Monitor cloud environments (primarily AWS) for security posture drift: misconfigured IAM roles, overly permissive security groups, exposed storage, and non-compliant resource configurations. Secure Kubernetes clusters and containerized workloads: manage Network Policies, RBAC, Admission Controllers, and runtime detection for anomalous container behavior. Develop and enforce cloud security policies and standards for AWS infrastructure, ensuring secure and scalable deployments align with organizational risk posture. Evaluate and lead the implementation of additional detection tooling, including cloud SIEM platforms, designing detection rules and alerting pipelines. Manage infrastructure as code (IaC) security using Terraform or OpenTofu — ensuring IaC definitions meet security standards before deployment. Automate security posture checks and detection workflows using Python and shell scripting. Stay current with the evolving cloud threat landscape and translate emerging threats into detection coverage or posture improvements. What You Bring Minimum 8 years of experience in cloud security, security engineering, or a related infrastructure security discipline. Hands-on experience with a cloud security posture management (CSPM) platform — CrowdStrike, Wiz, Prisma Cloud, Orca, or equivalent. Prior CrowdStrike experience is a plus but not required. Deep familiarity with AWS security architecture: IAM/SCP policy design, VPC networking, security groups, CloudTrail, and cloud-native security controls. GCP or Azure experience considered in lieu of AWS for strong candidates willing to expand into AWS. Proficiency with infrastructure as code (IaC) tools such as Terraform, OpenTofu, or CloudFormation, with an understanding of how to enforce security standards within IaC workflows. Strong Python and shell scripting skills for security automation, detection rule development, and tooling integration. Must be a US Citizen or legal permanent resident (Xometry handles ITAR-controlled data). Preferred AWS GovCloud experience. Hands-on Kubernetes security experience: securing and managing production clusters, including Network Policies, RBAC, and Admission Controllers. Experience with cloud-native SIEM solutions, including writing detection rules in Python or SQL. Experience securing microservices architectures, including service mesh security (Istio or Linkerd). Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field The estimated base salary range for new hires into this role is $180,000- $200,000 annually + bonus depending on factors such as job-related skills, relevant experience, and location. descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. You will be the primary technical architect for our landmark partnership with a major enterprise partner. This is not a standard plug-in project; you will be responsible for extracting Xometry’s core AI engines (DFM and IQE) and natively embedding them into our partner's core digital ecosystems. Your work will enable a "science fiction speed" workflow where designers receive real-time manufacturability and pricing feedback on native 3D geometry without ever leaving their primary design environment. This role requires a hybrid schedule (3 days a week) at our North Bethesda, MD or Waltham, MA office location. You'll introduce best practices for handling native 3D geometry data flows and ensure our systems are extensible, scalable, and capable of delivering real-time AI insights at the moment of design. AI Fluency: You will leverage AI tools to accelerate the development of geometry-processing pipelines and collaborate with our Data Science team to ensure the "IQE" (Instant Quoting) engine performs with sub-second latency within the partner application UI. In addition, you’ll define and evangelize the organization's AI fluency standards, coaching Staff and Senior engineers on integrating AI tooling into architecture, design, and development workflows to drive measurable productivity and quality outcomes. Problem Solving and Decision Making: You will tackle complex issues involving deep technical coupling between Xometry’s marketplace and our partner's enterprise software environment. You'll exercise judgment in selecting the right methods for ring-fenced data governance and "one-click" order placement within enterprise-grade security constraints. Scope and Impact: You are responsible for leading cross-team decision-making and executing multi-quarter roadmaps. Collaboration and Communication: You will act as the primary technical point of contact for our partner's engineering teams. You'll motivate internal Xometry teams to embrace the vision of a "unified digital thread" and mentor senior and mid-level engineers through complex design reviews. title: Senior Data Scientist, Product Analytics
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Xometry is looking for a highly analytical and data-driven Senior Data Scientist (Product Analytics) with statistical skills and a passion for data to drive improvements in technology. This role will be pivotal in leveraging data to optimize product performance, drive strategic decisions, and continuously improve our user experience through rigorous testing. You will delve deeply into product data, design and analyze experiments, and provide actionable insights that directly impact our product roadmap. Part of the scope of this role is measuring, experimenting on, and quantifying the impact of one of Xometry's highest-leverage strategic initiatives: the DFM AI + IQE integration with our partner. You will design the metric framework, experimentation strategy, and reporting that tell us whether the embedded experience inside the partner’s ecosystem - Designcenter, and Teamcenter — is actually delivering the "science fiction speed" digital thread from ideation to delivery, and how to make it better. How You’ll Contribute: Advanced Analytics: Conduct comprehensive analysis of product usage, user behavior, and performance metrics to identify opportunities for improvement Experimentation Design & Management: Design, implement, and manage A/B tests, causal analysis, and other experiments. Define clear hypotheses, target segments, and success metrics Experimentation Analysis: Analyze experiment results using statistical methods, providing detailed reports and recommendations. Identify statistically significant findings and translate them into actionable insights Integration Measurement: Own the measurement and experimentation strategy for the embedded DFM AI + IQE integration with our partner. Define success metrics and instrumentation across the in-CAD experience (Solid Edge, NX, Designcenter) and the Xometry marketplace, design cross-surface experiments and causal analyses that join the two funnels, work through the identity-resolution, attribution, and statistical-power challenges of low-volume enterprise cohorts, and quantify the funnel from designer intent in Teamcenter to manufactured part — making the digital thread's business impact legible to leadership. KPI Definition & Tracking: Define key performance indicators (KPIs) and establish robust tracking and reporting mechanisms, including KPIs that make sense in a PLM/CAD context (e.g., time-from-design-to-quote, in-CAD-to-order conversion, designer adoption per seat) as well as in the marketplace Dashboarding & Visualization: Develop and maintain dashboards to visualize experiment results, key metrics, and trends, making data accessible and understandable to stakeholders Collaboration: Work closely with product managers, engineers, designers, machine learning scientists, and — for the Siemens integration — partner engineering teams to implement and iterate on experiment findings and product improvements Data Storytelling: Communicate complex data insights and experiment results clearly and compellingly to diverse audiences, including leadership Data Integrity: Ensure data accuracy and integrity for all analysis and experimentation, including the cross-system data flows that span the Siemens and Xometry surfaces Methodology Development: Contribute to the development and improvement of our experimentation methodologies and best practices, especially for partner-integrated and multi-surface products What You'll Bring to Xometry: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, Information Systems, Economics, or another quantitative discipline 6–8 years of relevant experience Strong proficiency in data analysis, statistical modeling, and data visualization Proven experience in designing, implementing, and analyzing A/B tests and other experiments Solid understanding of statistical significance and hypothesis testing SQL is a must. title: Staff Product Manager, Buyer Experience
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. About This Role Xometry is looking for a driven, curious and customer obsessed Staff Product Manager to join its Buyer Experience group. In this role, you will manage the enterprise market segment - large enterprises that use Xometry to get their custom parts manufactured. Enterprise buyers bring a unique set of problems to solve: very large orders, procurement systems, complex purchase orders, contract terms, security and compliance reviews, and multiple stakeholders on a single account. Your job is to design self-service and human-assisted experiences inside that complexity, so an enterprise buyer gets the same frictionless quoting and ordering experience as anyone else, without giving up the controls and process their organization requires. You will define a 6-12 month forward-looking strategy for the enterprise segment, secure cross-functional buy-in across engineering, design, data science, category management, marketing, sales, legal/compliance and customer success, and hold accountability for outcomes that make quoting and ordering with Xometry frictionless for large accounts. You will be given a metric and a problem space, not a fully scoped backlog. Comfort defining your own roadmap from ambiguous signals is a requirement, not a bonus. This role requires a hybrid schedule (3 days a week) at our Waltham, MA or North Bethesda, MD office location. How You'll Contribute Enterprise Ecosystem Growth: Own the enterprise quote-to-order funnel end to end, from procurement intake and account onboarding through repeat ordering. Run structured experiments on RFQ intake flows and multi-stakeholder approval steps, using the results to drive measurable lifts in enterprise activation, conversion, and account expansion, all while keeping the experience self-service or human assisted depending on the need. User Research and Insights: Get very close to our enterprise customers and deeply understand the needs of all user personas - the engineer who needs the part, the procurement lead who has to source the part and the compliance reviewer who has to sign off, and their needs do not always line up. Problem Discovery: Proactively identify and define new problem spaces across the enterprise buyer lifecycle that will solve complex pain points for customers and drive the growth of our enterprise business. Product Strategy and Roadmap: Define and own the product strategy and the roadmap, with clear outcomes and milestones you present to technical and non-technical audiences. Data-Driven Decisions and Accountability: Set desired outcomes and define KPIs for each initiative you run. Monitor results closely and adjust priorities in real time, synthesizing findings into clear narratives for technical and non-technical audiences alike. Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enablement: Secure alignment across engineering, design, data science, category management and marketing, and drive adoption of new capabilities through rollout strategy, in-app education, and customer communication. Build and Ship with AI Agents: Operate spec-first. Translate your experimentation roadmap into structured, machine-executable specs that AI agents (Claude, Cursor) can build against, and work hand-in-hand with marketing, design, engineering and product analytics to prototype, validate, and ship statistically sound changes fast. What You'll Bring to Xometry You would be a good fit with: 10+ years of experience in product management, including direct ownership of an enterprise B2B or two-sided marketplace product. Experience working with large enterprise customers and a track record of not just building features, but crafting solutions that fit into complex organizational structures and workflows. AI-native, with hands-on fluency in tools like Claude and Cursor, and a track record of using them to compress the path from idea to validated, shipped product change. Strong strategic and analytical skills, with a systems-thinking approach to managing complexity and trade-offs across multiple product areas. Comfort making decisions under ambiguity, based on limited information, translating a loosely defined problem into a testable hypothesis and a plan. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to align senior leadership and cross-functional partners without direct authority. Proven ability to drive change within a fast-paced, scaling organization. Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Signals we look for You can walk through a specific enterprise feature or workflow you redesigned: the friction you removed, and the before and after numbers, not just the shipped feature. You have designed a product experience on a marketplace or B2B platform that supported large enterprise buyers with multiple personas whose needs did not always line up. You have shipped an ML or AI powered feature into a complex flow with multiple organizational hierarchies. You have worked on manufacturing, supply chain, or logistics products, or you can show how you learn unfamiliar operational domains fast. Pace: This is a startup pace inside a public company. You will be given a metric and an open problem, not a scoped project plan, and you will be expected to quickly move from hypothesis to shipped test. descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. AI Fluency: You will lead the effort to integrate production ML pipelines into the application layer, ensuring the "science fiction speed" promised in our vision is realized through optimized model serving and real-time geometry analysis. In addition, you’ll champion AI-assisted development practices across the team, actively mentoring engineers on effective use of AI tools to accelerate delivery, improve code quality, and reduce toil. Problem Solving and Decision Making: You will solve significant and unique challenges regarding data gravity and security. descriptionText: Senior Manufacturing Engineer - Onsite East Longmeadow, MA USA Come make the world and accelerate your success. It takes great people to achieve greatness. Join our top-notch team of approximately 43,500 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®. Review and improve existing manufacturing processes and equipment. Ensure that equipment, processes, and tooling, operate at satisfactory levels. Perform process capability studies. Identify and implement safety and productivity improvements. Participate in lean manufacturing initiatives that support continuous process improvements. Document work standards and instructions. Investigate production concerns. Perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions. Identify new equipment, processes, and tooling. Oversee procurement, plant layout, installations, and validations. Initiate capital budget requests. Plan, justify, and implement manufacturing proposals. Participate in the development and implementation of preventative maintenance programs. Ensure compliance with all EH&S policies as defined by Stanley Black & Decker, OSHA, and other regulatory agencies. Work cohesively within our team environment, participating in various projects and events to support the Plant’s needs. Engage with personnel from other departments and disciplines to successfully drive and complete tasks. The Person: You love to learn and grow and be acknowledged for your valuable contributions. You’re not intimidated by innovation. Wouldn’t it be great if you could do your job and do a world of good? In fact, you embrace it. You also have: 5+ years relevant engineering experience Related experience with process equipment, steel machining and welding Skilled in hands on equipment troubleshooting and process improvements Excellent project management skills Good analytical and problem solving skills Computer literate in Microsoft Office software and CAD The Details: You’ll receive a competitive salary and a great benefits plan, including: Medical, dental, life, vision, disability, 401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, paid time off, and tuition reimbursement in addition to programs & benefits in support of your well-being. Discounts on Stanley Black & Decker tools and other partner programs. And More: We want our company to be a place you’ll want to be – and stay. Learn: Have access to a wealth of learning resources, including our digital learning portal. As successful as we’ve been in the past, we have so much further to go. That’s where you come in. Join us! Your ideas and solutions have the potential to reach millions of customers as we work together to write the next chapter in our history. Come build with us and take your career to new heights. À propos du poste McKesson est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage). Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe. Ce que vous ferez Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle. Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données. Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données. Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance. Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance. Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données. Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue. Adaptability and curiosity with systems and technology, and eagerness to use tools to work more efficiently and reduce manual effort. Experience in reviewing contracts, along with familiarity with entertainment, media, or licensing accounting, is advantageous. descriptionText: We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. This is your chance to shape legendary play that lasts a lifetime. The Global Trade Compliance Analyst plays an integral role in supporting Hasbro’s global compliance program by conducting restricted party screening investigations, strengthening compliance processes, and supporting trade operations across LATAM markets. This position combines analytical rigor, operational execution, and cross-functional teamwork to mitigate risk, improve data accuracy, and enhance the efficient flow of goods. This is a high-visibility role that partners closely with leadership and cross-functional collaborators to drive continuous improvement, ensure regulatory adherence, and support strategic compliance initiatives. Key Responsibilities Investigate potential matches arising from denied party and sanctions screening systems, applying good judgment and regulatory knowledge with minimal guidance to support business continuity while ensuring compliance. Stay current on global sanctions regulations and denied party lists, providing interpretation and guidance to impacted collaborators. Support internal and external audits, including government inquiries, by providing insights and documentation. Conduct root cause analysis to identify process inefficiencies and drive improvements in data accuracy and workflow efficiency. Support the development, standardization, and implementation of policies, procedures, and key performance indicators, and track compliance metrics and reporting to support leadership decision-making. Support critical initiatives focused on compliance enhancements, cost reduction, and operational efficiency, including participation in system testing, integration efforts, and continuous improvement projects. Partner with internal teams including Legal/Compliance, Logistics, Security, and Internal Audit to support trade compliance initiatives. Act as a consultative partner to global business units to ensure alignment with trade compliance requirements. LATAM Trade Compliance Support In addition to core screening responsibilities, this role provides operational and analytical support across LATAM markets, including: Tariff Classification Support: Assist with classification activities by compiling product data, maintaining records, and supporting periodic reviews of duty rates and product categories. Customs Broker Coordination: Support the validation of broker-assigned classifications by gathering documentation, tracking feedback, and calling out discrepancies. Post-Entry Audit Support: Assist with post-entry reviews by compiling documentation, validating declared data (e.g., classification, valuation), and supporting corrective actions. Data Management & Reporting: Maintain compliance trackers, support data validation efforts, and ensure accurate and complete recordkeeping. Process & SOP Support: Assist in updating and maintaining Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure consistency across markets. Regional Projects: Provide support for regional compliance initiatives and process improvement efforts. Additional Responsibilities Conduct self-audits to ensure alignment with corporate policies and regulatory requirements. Participate in trade compliance training programs and actively contribute to risk reduction and process improvements. Required Qualifications & Skills Experience within the area of trade compliance, customs, or international logistics/operations preferred. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, paired with the capacity to handle complex investigations independently. Excellent organization, time management, and prioritization skills in a fast-paced, global environment. Proactive, detail-oriented, and highly self-motivated. Advanced Excel skills and the ability to quickly learn new systems and tools. English and Spanish language proficiency preferred. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required. Trade compliance or international logistics experience is a plus. Travel 10–15% travel (as needed) Hasbro is committed to equality of opportunity in all aspects of employment. We are committed to making all employment decisions

title: Analyste principal(e) de la sécurité SAP
descriptionText: We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. À propos du poste Hasbro est à la recherche d'un(e) analyste principal(e) de la sécurité SAP pour se joindre à son équipe de sécurité TI à Montréal. Ce poste de contributeur(trice) individuel(le) senior jouera un rôle clé dans la gouvernance des accès, le développement des rôles, la conformité et les contrôles de sécurité au sein des environnements SAP ECC, S/4HANA, SAP RISE, SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), Identity Authentication Service (IAS) et Identity Provisioning Service (IPS). Alors que nous rapatrions davantage de responsabilités liées à la sécurité SAP à l'interne, nous recherchons une personne capable de diriger des initiatives complexes grâce à son expertise, sa collaboration et son jugement. Ce poste ne comporte aucune responsabilité de gestion de personnel, mais il offre une orientation technique aux analystes SAP, aux administrateurs des accès, aux équipes de projet, aux partenaires d'affaires, aux auditeurs ainsi qu'aux partenaires d'implantation. Vos principales responsabilités Concevoir et faire évoluer l'architecture de sécurité SAP, les normes, les modèles d'accès et les pratiques de conception des rôles. Soutenir la migration vers SAP RISE, notamment en ce qui concerne le mappage des rôles, l'intégration des identités, la transition des accès, les accès privilégiés, la connectivité et les contrôles post-migration. Développer et améliorer les modèles de contrôle d'accès basé sur les rôles (RBAC) afin de respecter le principe du moindre privilège, de répondre aux besoins de l'entreprise et de satisfaire aux exigences de conformité. Diriger les initiatives de nettoyage, de refonte et de simplification des rôles ainsi que la remédiation des conflits liés à la séparation des tâches (SoD). Configurer et administrer SAP Identity Access Governance (IAG) et SAP Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), y compris les connecteurs, les flux de travail, les règles de risque, l'approvisionnement des accès, l'analyse des accès et les rapports. Renforcer les processus d'attribution des accès, les revues périodiques des accès ainsi que la gouvernance des accès d'urgence et des accès privilégiés. Soutenir les exigences SOX et les contrôles généraux TI (ITGC) en recueillant les preuves d'audit, en participant aux revues d'audit, en résolvant les écarts et en produisant une documentation claire. Évaluer les risques liés aux accès, les rôles mal conçus, les conflits de séparation des tâches, les configurations non sécurisées et les lacunes de contrôle. Collaborer avec les équipes des finances, de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, des ressources humaines, des achats, des applications SAP, de l'architecture d'entreprise, de la gestion des identités, de la cybersécurité, de la conformité, de l'audit ainsi qu'avec les partenaires externes. Offrir un mentorat technique et guider les équipes sans responsabilité officielle de gestion. Ce que vous apporterez De 6 à 8 ans ou plus d'expérience en sécurité SAP, gouvernance des accès, développement des rôles ou dans un domaine connexe. Solide compréhension des concepts d'autorisation SAP ECC et SAP S/4HANA. Expérience dans la configuration ou le soutien de SAP GRC et de SAP Identity Access Governance (IAG). Bonne connaissance des considérations de sécurité liées à SAP BTP, IAS, IPS et SAP RISE. Connaissance des principes de contrôle d'accès basé sur les rôles (RBAC), de la séparation des tâches (SoD), de la gestion des accès privilégiés, de la gestion du cycle de vie des utilisateurs et des revues d'accès. Expérience de soutien aux activités liées à SOX, aux contrôles généraux TI (ITGC), aux audits internes ou externes. Capacité à piloter des initiatives complexes, à communiquer efficacement et à établir des relations de confiance avec des partenaires techniques et d'affaires. Atouts Certification SAP en sécurité ou toute autre certification SAP pertinente. Expérience en sécurisation d'environnements SAP RISE hébergés sur AWS ou dans une infrastructure infonuagique gérée par SAP. Expérience de migrations vers SAP S/4HANA, de modernisation d'ERP, d'environnements SAP hybrides ou d'intégration des identités infonuagiques. Expérience de la gestion des accès d'urgence, des campagnes de certification des accès, de l'automatisation de l'approvisionnement des accès et des contrôles des accès privilégiés. Expérience dans une entreprise d'envergure mondiale comportant des processus d'affaires complexes et des exigences d'audit importantes. title: Applied AI Engineer
descriptionText: We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. At Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, you’ll collaborate with passionate teams to reimagine our iconic brands and create experiences that spark joy, connection, and community through the magic of play. This is your chance to shape legendary play that lasts a lifetime. We're building something new inside our AI Studio, and we're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to help shape it with us. This role sits at the center of a new and constantly evolving set of challenges. The problems are still being defined, and the approaches are actively being invented. What excites us is the opportunity to determine what it truly means for an iconic character to think, respond, and stay true to itself - consistently, safely, and at scale. We work where storytelling, imagination, and technology converge. Our focus is on the intelligence layer: the systems that determine how characters understand context, form responses, maintain a consistent voice, and hold carefully defined boundaries. This is where canon knowledge meets language model behavior, and where the quality of every character interaction gets defined and measured. This role owns one of the most creatively and technically interesting areas on the team: making characters that actually feel like themselves. Working closely with engineers, creative partners, and brand leaders, the Applied AI Engineer will define prompt architecture, own guardrails and evaluation frameworks, and build the retrieval systems that ground characters in their own lore. Success here means developing the tools and practices that make character fidelity measurable. What You'll Do Design, implement, and continuously refine system prompts, character behavior definitions, and guardrails for our AI character platform. Build evaluation frameworks to measure character fidelity, response quality, and safety — establishing quantitative standards for what "in character" actually means across interaction types. Architect and implement RAG systems to ground character responses in canonical knowledge, including embedding strategies, vector retrieval, and relevance evaluation. Partner with creative and brand teams to translate character attributes — personality, voice, canon, tone, and boundaries — into precise, testable AI behavior and system requirements. Lead prompt versioning, regression testing, and model evaluation practices to ensure character behavior remains consistent across provider updates and model changes. Integrate with multi-provider LLM APIs (OpenAI, Google Gemini, etc.) and make principled selection decisions as the landscape evolves. Evaluate and adopt emerging techniques in prompt engineering, agentic design, and LLM evaluation that meaningfully advance the quality and reliability of character experiences. What You Will Bring 3+ years of experience building and shipping production LLM-powered systems. Deep expertise in prompt engineering — system prompt design, few-shot techniques, chain-of-thought, multi-turn conversation management, and structured output. Experience designing and implementing evaluation frameworks for LLM outputs, including adversarial and security testing. Hands-on experience with RAG architectures: embedding models, vector stores, chunking strategies, and retrieval evaluation. Proficiency with major LLM APIs (OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, or equivalent) and experience making principled decisions between them. Strong Python skills and comfort working in AWS environments. Familiarity with how voice AI services work (TTS, STT) — enough to understand how spoken delivery shapes prompt and response design. The ability to communicate AI system behavior clearly to creative, brand, and non-technical collaborators. Extra Credit Familiarity with guardrails frameworks (NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, or equivalent). Conceptual understanding of fine-tuning and RLHF, even if not a primary area of focus. PURPOSE OF THE ROLE The Integrated Supply Chain Manager owns the end-to-end demand-to-delivery cycle for the market, bringing together demand planning/S&OP and logistics/order management into a single point of accountability. The role supports overall business revenue and profit delivery through rigorous management of demand signals across product and customer channels, and through efficient logistics, fulfilment and order management execution. The role partners Commercial leadership and works across multi-functional teams — Sales, Marketing, Finance, Logistics and Supply Planning — to assure alignment and sufficiency in the business plans to deliver anticipated demand, while ensuring smooth supply chain operations and best-in-class customer service. This is a hands-on leadership role at an inflection point. The platform has grown organically alongside the business, and we're now ready to be far more intentional about it: fewer, better-supported capabilities; clearer standards; a simpler operating footprint. You'll lead a team of platform engineers through that evolution, setting technical direction, growing the people on the team, and building the organizational alignment that makes real change stick. If you're energized by taking capable platforms and turning them into a coherent product that other teams love using, this role is for you. What You'll Do: LEAD AND GROW THE TEAM Manage, coach, and develop a team of data platform engineers spanning early-career through senior levels. Run a healthy engineering practice: clear priorities and process, diligent code review, sustainable support, and blameless retrospectives that produce continuous improvement. Own hiring and team design as the platform's scope grows, assessing where you need depth or breadth and making great hires. Create development paths for your engineers, and establish real ownership of the platform and its components within the team. SET PLATFORM STRATEGY AND DRIVE STANDARDIZATION Treat the platform as a product: define what we offer, who it serves, what's supported, and what isn't. Establish a set of standard, well-documented platform offerings - the default path most teams should take - and drive adoption across data engineering, analytics, and AI. Assess the current tooling landscape, identify where capabilities overlap or duplicate one another, and build a prioritized plan to consolidate onto a smaller, better-supported set. Own the full lifecycle of platform capabilities, including the harder work: deprecating what we no longer want to support and shepherding consumers through migration. Balance central standards against genuine team-specific needs, and know when to hold the line versus grant a well-reasoned exception. OWN THE TARGET-STATE ARCHITECTURE Develop a clear, defensible point of view on where our data platform architecture should land, and build alignment behind it with engineering leadership and partner teams. Lead the team through significant platform evolution - consolidating overlapping capabilities, simplifying our cloud footprint, and migrating workloads between environments - with minimal disruption to the teams that depend on us. Make and document architectural decisions with explicit reasoning on cost, capability, operational burden, and long-term maintainability. Guide the team's infrastructure-as-code practice (Terraform) so that platform changes are reviewable, repeatable, and reversible. DRIVE RELIABILITY, PERFORMANCE, AND COST DISCIPLINE Own the reliability of the data platform: monitoring, alerting, incident response, and the improvements that reduce recurrence. Establish the operational metrics that matter — availability, pipeline freshness, query performance, cost per workload — and manage the team against them. Own platform spend. FinOps is important here - you should understand where the money goes, forecast it credibly, and make deliberate tradeoffs between cost and capability. Hold a high bar for documentation, runbooks, and operational readiness as a condition of shipping. Demonstrated experience leading technical change through influence: bringing stakeholders along, sequencing migrations so no team gets stranded, and sustaining momentum on multi-quarter efforts. Hands-on depth with modern cloud data platforms. Direct experience with Databricks and/or Snowflake, and the judgment to evaluate platforms against each other on cost, capability, and operational fit rather than preference. Strong AWS experience. Experience operating in — or migrating away from — other major clouds is valuable context. Practical experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform preferred) and Git-based CI/CD workflows. Solid SQL and working proficiency in Python or a comparable language. Experience owning production reliability for data infrastructure, including on-call, incident command, and post-incident follow-through. Practical experience with data access governance: provisioning and deprovisioning, entitlement review, data classification, credential rotation, and audit logging you'd be comfortable putting in front of an auditor. Working understanding of what AI and ML workloads need from a data platform, including how agents and internal services should get governed, least-privilege access to platform data and tools (MCP or comparable patterns). Clear written communication. Much of this role is making a technical case legible to people who don't read code. NICE TO HAVE Experience consolidating or rationalizing a fragmented tooling landscape onto a smaller set of supported offerings. Experience leading a substantial cloud or data warehouse migration, including the change management around it. Data governance or access management experience at scale in a multi-region or compliance-constrained environment. title: Strategic Partnerships Director
descriptionText: ABOUT CAREMESSAGE CareMessage is a social enterprise and the largest patient engagement platform for low-income populations in the United States. We deliver personalized health education and care coordination through text messaging — reaching patients where they already are, in the language they speak, at the moments that matter most. Unlike technology built for large health systems and adapted down, CareMessage is designed from the ground up for organizations serving low-income, historically marginalized communities. WHY JOIN US IN LEVERAGING TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE HEALTH EQUITY Many of us have had the experience of doing good work or building great products, but wondering if it is truly making an impact. At CareMessage, our mission is clear: improve health equity for low-income populations across the United States. Every role here connects directly to that purpose. We care deeply about the communities we serve, and we also hold a high standard for performance, collaboration, and integrity. Our ideal team members: - Deliver meaningful, measurable results - Invest in their teammates and build trust - Seek feedback and continually grow - Stay steady and solutions-oriented in ambiguity - Lead with integrity and responsibility - Communicate with clarity and empathy If you are motivated by impact, energized by collaboration, and ready to do some of the most meaningful work of your career, we encourage you to apply. If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you. _____________________________________ ABOUT THE ROLE CareMessage is hiring a Strategic Partnerships Director to build the partnership operating layer that helps our Growth team scale revenue, reach, and patient impact through a disciplined, measurable, and mission-aligned ecosystem strategy. The ideal candidate for this role is one that is not only motivated by driving ARR, but sees equal value in what partnerships translate into in terms of patient impact. This will be a highly cross-functional individual contributor role that needs to help the organization achieve revenue targets through partnerships. As a social enterprise and patient engagement platform designed for low-income, historically marginalized communities, CareMessage grows by helping safety-net organizations engage patients, increase access to care, improve clinical outcomes, and address social drivers of health. This role will translate that mission into a clearer partnership system that supports our current FQHC business, partner-led market expansion through Tribal Health and other organizations, and mission-aligned organization acquisition through Free & Charitable Clinic Associations. This is an L4 individual contributor role with broad cross-departmental ownership. The Strategic Partnerships Director will not manage direct reports at this stage; instead, they will orchestrate partnership execution across Growth, Product, Customer Experience, Professional Services, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Marketing, and Strategy so that partnerships move from relationship activity into measurable revenue, market access, operating discipline, and patient impact. This role will own partner-driven and partner-influenced ARR outcomes, build the systems needed to make partner contribution visible and accountable, and support CareMessage’s work to drive impact in key regions like Texas and other ecosystem-based growth opportunities. Success in this role means creating joint value: measurable growth for CareMessage, clear value for the partner, and meaningful access, engagement, workflow, or outcome improvement for the safety-net organizations and patients we serve. WHAT YOU WILL DO A. OWN PARTNER-DRIVEN AND PARTNER-INFLUENCED OUTCOMES THAT DRIVE OUR GROWTH - Own the partnership operating plan for CareMessage’s partnership growth work, including partner-driven ARR, partner-influenced ARR, partner-generated sales-accepted pipeline, attribution rules, partner portfolio priorities, and patient-impact narrative. - Translate CareMessage’s partnership strategy into quarterly execution priorities across platform, network, association, and regional ecosystem partners, with focus on key partners and regions like Texas and other priority market-entry motions. - Orchestrate cross-departmental execution with Sales, Product, Customer Experience, Professional Services, Finance, RevOps, Legal, Compliance, and Marketing so partner opportunities move from signal to qualified opportunity, signed agreement, launch, measured adoption, and ARR or impact outcome. - Use partner performance, pipeline quality, attribution, implementation readiness, product or technical dependencies, and customer / patient impact signals to recommend where CareMessage should invest, reset, scale, or sunset partnerships, including communicating risks, tradeoffs, resource needs, and decisions to the Chief Growth Officer through clear, data-driven updates that include cross-functional implications. B. LEAD CROSS-DEPARTMENTAL PARTNERSHIP EXECUTION ACROSS OUR DIVERSE PARTNERSHIPS PORTFOLIO - Lead the operating rhythm for priority partnerships across EHR and platform partners, API/interoperability partners, data and workflow partners, referral and co-sell partners, PCAs/HCCNs, networks, payers, ACOs/CINs, funders, and sponsored-program partners by strengthening owners, decision rights, milestones, risk checkpoints, handoffs, and executive decisions needed to move from partner interest to signed agreement, launch, and measurable growth or impact. - Convert partner opportunities into mutual plans that clarify joint value for CareMessage, the partner, and the customer or patient, including commercial model, co-sell or referral motion, product and implementation needs, legal and compliance requirements, and success measures. - Hold internal and external stakeholders accountable to agreed partnership milestones by surfacing blockers, resolving cross-functional tradeoffs, and escalating decisions when partnership execution depends on company-level choices. - Ensure partnership commitments are feasible and durable by validating product, technical, implementation, financial, data/privacy, and support implications before CareMessage makes market-facing promises. C. BUILD REPEATABLE AND SCALABLE PARTNER MOTIONS AND OPERATING SYSTEMS ACROSS OUR PARTNERSHIPS PORTFOLIO - Build repeatable partner motions across referral, co-sell, marketplace, sponsored-program, association, network, and integration-enabled pathways, with clear criteria for when each model should be used. - Create the partnership operating system, including partner segmentation, rules of engagement, mutual plans, handoff workflows, scorecards, QBRs, attribution, and success criteria, so partner contribution is visible and repeatable. - Strengthen decision rules for investing, maintaining, resetting, scaling, or sunsetting partnerships based on strategic fit, partner-sourced or partner-influenced pipeline, ARR impact, implementation burden, product dependency, and patient impact. - Use AI, automation, CRM/PRM workflows, dashboards, and meeting intelligence to reduce manual coordination, improve follow-through, synthesize partner signals, and make partnership performance inspectable. WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE WITHIN 30 DAYS: LEARN, MAP, AND ALIGN - Build a current-state map of CareMessage’s partner portfolio, including active relationships, stalled relationships, emerging opportunities, partner economics, risks, and open commitments. - Propose and align with the Chief Growth Officer and key cross-functional leaders on partner-driven and partner-influenced ARR definitions, priority relationships, decision rights, and operating cadence. - Identify the highest-priority partner relationships to invest in, reset, pause, or clarify based on strategic fit, revenue potential, patient impact, and internal capacity. Unlike technology built for large health systems and adapted down, CareMessage is designed from the ground up for organizations serving low-income, historically marginalized communities. WHY JOIN US IN LEVERAGING TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE HEALTH EQUITY Many of us have had the experience of doing good work or building great products, but wondering if it is truly making an impact. At CareMessage, our mission is clear: improve health equity for low-income populations across the United States. Every role here connects directly to that purpose. We care deeply about the communities we serve, and we also hold a high standard for performance, collaboration, and integrity. Our ideal team members: - Deliver meaningful, measurable results - Invest in their teammates and build trust - Seek feedback and continually grow - Stay steady and solutions-oriented in ambiguity - Lead with integrity and responsibility - Communicate with clarity and empathy If you are motivated by impact, energized by collaboration, and ready to do some of the most meaningful work of your career, we encourage you to apply. If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you. _____________________________________ ROLE OVERVIEW The Engineering Manager, Data & Clinical Integration owns and drives the technical direction of the two teams responsible for CareMessage's data — the Clinical Integration team, which connects CareMessage to electronic health records (EHRs) and other clinical data sources (e.g. HIEs, Payor Data, etc.) across our customer base, and the Data team, which turns that data into trustworthy insights. CareMessage supports over 400 safety-net healthcare organizations including federally qualified health centers and free clinics that care for low-income and underserved patients nationwide, and these two teams are the engine behind our ability to measurably demonstrate impact on clinical outcomes, access to care, and the social drivers of health. This is a leadership role over existing teams: their systems and roadmaps are already in place, and your job is to lead, deepen, and scale them. A core part of this role is leading both teams to turn clinical data from our customers' many different EHRs into trustworthy, query-ready data that can measurably demonstrate health outcomes — and scaling those insights through both AI/ML and human analysis. The Clinical Integration team builds and maintains the integrations that connect CareMessage to leading EHRs (Epic, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, AthenaHealth, and others) over HL7, FHIR, Proprietary APIs, and direct-database interfaces using the Rhapsody integration engine, and it owns the first step of the clinical data pipeline — converting clinical data to FHIR and landing it in our FHIR Store and BigQuery. The Data team builds on top of that with a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture in BigQuery using native Google Cloud services, and dbt, surfacing insights through Metabase dashboards such as our Health Equity and diabetes-outcomes views; and increasingly powering AI/ML-driven workflows that surface insights at scale. In this role, you will collaborate closely with Product, Customer Success, Data, Compliance, and Engineering to design and deliver the platform and integrations that deepen patient engagement and health outcomes, with direct ownership of technical decisions and customer-facing system behavior. Our ideal candidate is an experienced Engineering Manager (technical, people and process leader) who thrives in dynamic, fully-distributed environments and is energized by the intersection of healthcare interoperability and data. They are passionate about partnering with business stakeholders to develop the platform and processes that uncover data insights, and they are dedicated to the professional growth of engineers. They view themselves as a catalyst for organizational outcomes and accomplish that through enabling high-output team productivity and continuously seek ways to elevate Engineering and the organization as a whole. Above all, they share our mission-driven commitment and take pride in contributing to our objective of advancing health equity for low-income populations. One of the strongest skills we value here is taking a scientific approach to everything we do. We rely on evidence alongside intuition, and we look for data that challenges our assumptions before drawing conclusions. Our PRDs, documentation, and wikis reflect this mindset — we use data to guide decisions and validate our work. CORE REQUIREMENTS - Proven Track Record: At least 5 years of successful experience as an Engineering Manager over Integration and/or Data Engineering teams, in two or more early-to-growth-stage remote startup environments. - Strategic Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead and drive the delivery of long-term technical projects across multiple teams driving measurable outcomes. - Technical Proficiency: Strong technical acumen with a deep understanding of SQL, data concepts, pipelines (ELT), and cloud data warehousing. - Modern & AI-Assisted Engineering: A track record of adopting modern development practices and leveraging AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Agentic coding, harnesses, and LLM-based workflows) to raise engineering velocity and quality — with the judgment to apply them responsibly in a healthcare/PHI context. You actively coach your teams to fold these tools into their day-to-day work. - Hands-on Experience: The ability to get hands-on with SQL and data tooling when needed. (This is predominantly a management position; however, you should be able to dig in to help answer key data questions and unblock the team.) - Collaborative Expertise: Exceptional collaboration and influencing skills, working effectively cross-departmentally to craft optimal solutions while navigating multiple constraints. - Situational Awareness: The ability to discern when to dive into technical details and when to maintain a higher-level perspective when working with Engineers, Product, and Design. - Cultural Advocate: A commitment to cultivating both individual growth and a high-performance engineering culture that attracts top talent. - Mentorship: A growth-oriented mindset with the capability to guide others on their development journey. - Communication Skills: Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, especially in a fully remote environment. - Autonomous Prioritization: Proficiency in identifying and managing priorities independently across two teams, ensuring an efficient workflow. - Diversity and Inclusion: Dedication to promoting diversity and inclusion within teams, especially given our global team composition. - This role requires the candidate to reside within the United States of America. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE - Experience managing or working closely with healthcare integration / interoperability teams (HL7, FHIR) in addition to Data teams. - Experience working in a Healthcare technology environment and the requisite Security and Compliance requirements (HIPAA/PHI). - Experience introducing or scaling agentic development workflows on a team, with attention to code quality, security, and compliance. - Experience applying AI/ML to large datasets to scale insight generation (e.g., summarization, classification, anomaly detection). - Experience with our Tech Stack: - Data: GCP / BigQuery, dbt, Python, Metabase, and a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture. - Clinical Integration: Rhapsody integration engine (JavaScript), HL7, FHIR, FHIR Store, mainstream EHRs (Epic, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, AthenaHealth), Ruby on Rails, Postgres, GCP. - Background in TDD engineering environments. - Experience leveraging healthcare data and foundational data science concepts. review and collaborate with engineers on technical specifications to ensure excellence in execution. - Work closely with Product and Design to conceptualize and define impactful solutions, often through Product Requirements Documents (PRDs). - Skillfully lead and facilitate team rituals such as Kickoffs, Retrospectives, and Tech Debt Reviews, and collaborate cross-functionally to understand estimates and prioritize the backlog, making pragmatic trade-offs. - Develop processes, tools, and systems that enhance the departments' overall effectiveness. - Contribute to the team by participating in the On-Call (PagerDuty) rotation. WITHIN 1 MONTH YOU'LL: - Gain a foundational understanding of our product, customers, and patients. - Meet key internal stakeholders and begin to understand policies and protocols (including our Security and Compliance posture). - Establish rapport with the engineers on both teams through Wiki contributions, 1:1s, and team rituals as well as with key peer collaborators (e.g. Product) - Develop a working understanding of the clinical data pipeline — from EHR integration through the medallion architecture and reporting. WITHIN 3 MONTHS YOU'LL: - Complete a product demo, demonstrating your comprehension of our overall product platform. - Gain a strong understanding of our technical environment and identify areas for growth in our processes, systems, and/or tooling. - Take over responsibility for performance management and feedback for the engineers you oversee. - Have a clear, shared roadmap across the Data and Clinical Integration teams, with healthy dependency management between them. - Have implemented at least one improvement that impacts the way all of Engineering operates. WITHIN 6 MONTHS YOU'LL: - Display strong leadership across both teams and within engineering management as a whole. - Have a deep understanding of our data platform and clinical integration landscape, and refine the technical roadmap and sequencing to meet our long-term data goals while ensuring compliance with all necessary requirements. - Work with engineering leadership to recruit and hire best-in-class engineers as needed. - Make contributions to processes, tooling, or technology that impact the way the company operates. title: Chief Product and Technology Officer
descriptionText: ABOUT CAREMESSAGE CareMessage is a social enterprise and the largest patient engagement platform for low-income populations in the United States. If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you. _____________________________________ ABOUT THE ROLE CareMessage is seeking a Chief Product and Technology Officer who will decide where we place our product and technology bets, build the organization that delivers them, and prove that what we ship changes people’s health. Product management, product marketing, design, engineering, data and user research all report to this role, which replaces our outgoing Chief Technology Officer. We are a product-driven organization and have been since 2012. That describes how we decide, not whose work matters. Our engineering team built a platform that reaches millions of people reliably, integrates with the electronic health records our customers already use, and put an AI Assistant in the hands of frontline staff who kept using it. Three patents and 17 peer-reviewed studies sit behind our outcomes. The next build is harder, and you will need to be as serious about engineering as about product. The test of this seat is whether our strategy looks different because you are in it. You set the bets, how the organization is built to deliver them, and what we stop doing to make room. The Founders, in consultation with the Board, remain the authority on our mission, our values, and what health equity impact means here. Within that, the direction is yours. Other organizations leave the safety net as they scale. We go deeper into it. Our core operations are funded by our enterprise product, and philanthropy funds research into what comes next. Growing the core is what earns us the right to make bigger bets. More than anything, we want curiosity as a practice. Go find out. Be wrong out loud. Let what a clinic staff member tells you change your plan. The people we serve may be working two jobs, sharing a phone, or reading most easily in a language other than English. We can teach you this market. We cannot teach you to want to understand people whose lives look different from your own. WHAT YOU WILL DO A. BUILD THE ORGANIZATION’S CAPABILITIES TO DELIVER HEALTH EQUITY IMPACT THROUGH TECHNOLOGY 1. Lead, coach and develop 30+ people across product management, product marketing, design, software engineering, data, and user research, and grow those teams so they more directly own key outcomes that support how our organization intends to grow. Build the bench and succession beneath you so our capability outlasts any one leader. 2. Accelerate our organizational ability to deliver health equity impact. We were an early adopter of generative artificial intelligence and our AI Assistant is live and widely used by frontline staff. The larger opportunity is what this organization can achieve when we adapt innovative technologies both in our products and within our internal teams, so that we scale our impact without scaling our cost base proportionally. 3. Leverage our Board, advisors, and broader ecosystem as core enablers and force-multipliers. Tapping into their deep line of sight across healthcare and tech ensures we lock onto the highest-impact focus areas with speed. B. DECIDE WHERE CAREMESSAGE PLACES THE PRODUCT AND TECHNOLOGY BETS THAT MAXIMIZE IMPACT ON HEALTH EQUITY - Set the direction across access to care, clinical outcomes and the social drivers of health, toward demonstrating 5 million people had a measurable health equity improvement a year by 2028. Set the technical direction that delivers on this, grounding everything you do in what you learn from patients and safety-net staff, not in a playbook you brought with you. - Decide how we allocate. Every invested dollar lands in one of three places. Work that moves health equity outcomes, work that keeps us competitive in a crowded market and maintenance, and technical debt that keeps the platform standing. Push as much as you can into the first without letting the other two decay, and be plain with the Executive Team about what the split is and why you chose it. Deciding what we will not pursue is part of the same call. We hold several hypotheses about how to scale our impact, and the discipline is to test them without risking what funds us. - Related to the above, grow the enterprise product that funds our core operations and reaches our target populations at scale, and find the room that remains in the healthcare safety-net market. Our model is that philanthropy invents a capability and earned revenue keeps it, so deciding what has proven itself and is ready to graduate into the Core is part of this job. C. PROVE OUR PRODUCTS MEANINGFULLY SOLVE FOR HEALTH EQUITY OUTCOMES AND MAXIMIZE THEIR REACH 1. Own adoption. We serve 1 in 6 FQHCs and 1 in 7 Free and Charitable Clinics, alongside Tribal health organizations and their networks. But a signed contract is not an outcome because real impact requires active usage. Resource-constrained clinics will not adopt software just because it is good. Your job is to convert one-time campaigns into self-sustaining workflows and build low-touch paths so the smallest organizations succeed independently. Partnering with our Chief Growth Officer on pricing, packaging, and positioning, you will ensure no segment is left behind by balancing commercial growth with mission impact. 2. Own our intellectual property. Our core IP is behavior change, backed by patents on sequential messaging and 17 peer-reviewed studies. This makes us the only patient engagement platform with published clinical outcomes for low-income populations. You will direct our IP strategy: deciding what we protect, what we publish, and how we generate clinical evidence far faster than traditional trial cycles allow. 3. Own the technical partnerships and infrastructure. Patients navigate clinics, food banks, and housing programs that operate in silos. We build the connective tissue through deep EHR integrations, a unified cross-organization patient record, and scalable APIs that let new partners plug in without custom code. You will own our technical partner relationships and the underlying infrastructure that connects the safety net. WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE WITHIN 30 DAYS: BUILD A FIRST-HAND POINT OF VIEW ON HOW WE HAVE CHOSEN OUR ORGANIZATIONAL BETS 1. Build a durable practice for staying close to our users and use it immediately. By day 30 we expect you to name at least one assumption in our current plan that your own first-hand learning has already changed. 2. Deliver an honest read on the product and engineering organization: where the talent and leadership gaps sit, where the risks are, and what you would do about them in the next 60 days. 3. Build a working command of our strategy, our financial picture, and how enterprise product revenue funds our operations. WITHIN 60 DAYS: SET THE DIRECTION AND COMMIT THE ORGANIZATION TO IT 1. Deliver a first draft of the product and technology strategy to the CEO and Executive Team naming the bets worth making, the sequence, what we will decline to build, and how the stretch bets get tested without risking the Core. 2. Deliver a candid diagnostic of the product, the technical debt, and the organization's capacity to deliver against that strategy. 3. Agree with the Chief Growth Officer on one experiment in pricing, packaging or adoption that tests where room remains in the safety-net market. WITHIN 90 DAYS: DEVELOP A PLAN TO SUPPORT THE ORGANIZATION’S APPROACH TO TECHNOLOGY FOR HEALTH EQUITY 1. Move the direction from a document to a commitment: the bets funded and sequenced through 2027, a named owner against each, and the tradeoffs the Executive Team has accepted. By day 90, this organization should know what it is building, what it is not, and who is accountable. 2. Deliver a plan to accelerate how the team uses artificial intelligence and to strengthen technical leadership in the function, naming the gaps and how you will close them. 3. Outline your reasoning behind the two or three external technical/infrastructure partnerships most worth pursuing and/or deepening against our outcomes trajectory, and your plan to pursue/deepen them. KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS FOR THIS ROLE MAY INCLUDE: 1. Health equity outcomes we can prove at scale, meaning measurable clinical and social outcomes attributable to our products. 2. Adoption and reach among safety-net organizations with limited capacity to adopt anything, including a viable low-touch path for the smallest organizations, and the health of the enterprise product that funds our operations. 3. Organizational leverage, meaning the impact we produce per person and per dollar as we grow. We intend to scale what we deliver without scaling our cost base proportionally, and that depends on how well this organization uses technology internally rather than only inside product and engineering. Delivering at one to two dollars per patient per year is the standard we hold ourselves to, and the health and retention of the team that makes it possible is part of the same measure. WHAT YOU WILL BRING 1. You have run multiple functions together, and you can point to outcomes you owned rather than features your team shipped. You have set a direction an organization followed, presented to a board, and built people who went on to bigger jobs. 2. You have changed an engineering organization's technical direction without authority over it, and you can explain the argument well enough for an engineer to judge it. This one is not negotiable. 3. You are curious as a practice. You go find out. You are willing to be wrong out loud. Your view of patients and frontline staff came from being around them. 4. You want to go deeper into the safety net, not upmarket. Most product leaders build a career moving toward better-funded customers. This job runs the other way, and it will not suit someone who sees low-income populations as a stage. 5. You treat intellectual property as an asset rather than a legal formality, whether that is patents, published evidence, proprietary data, or all three. 6. descriptionText: Thanks for visiting our Career Page. Please review our open positions and apply to the positions that match your qualifications. AI Video Generation Architect Remote Full Time Innovation Experienced Share Start Date: ASAPRole Type: Full-Time, SalariedBackground: Software developmentLocation: Remote, Flexible (USA based)Salary: $170,000-$200,000 per year, plus benefitsWho We Are:The Modern Classrooms Project (MCP) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that empowers educators to build classrooms that respond to every student’s needs. Founded by two award-winning teachers, we lead a movement of educators in implementing a self-paced, mastery-based instructional model that leverages technology to foster human connection, authentic learning, and social-emotional growth.To date, we have reached over 100,000+ teachers through our free online course in 150+ countries. We are an ambitious, idealistic team led by former classroom teachers, and we are passionate about what we do. Job Description - Why we need you! Effective instructional videos make high-quality instruction accessible to all learners, regardless of experience or background. Every day, in classrooms around the world, Modern Classroom educators replace live lectures with instructional videos so that students can learn at their own paces, in school and/or at home. Good videos enhance learning — and they are time consuming to produce. A single high-quality lesson video can take hours to plan, record, edit, and caption.We need an experienced, hands-on, AI-native engineer to build a brand new, state-of-the-art generative pipeline that turns specifications into high-quality instructional videos — complete with animations, synchronized AI narration, captions, and automated ground-truth quality verification. You will own the video render path end to end, from the canonical specification to the final rendered output, creating intuitive, powerful tools that will directly support educators and students every day. Key ResponsibilitiesAs our AI Video Generation Architect, you will be a senior individual contributor on our Engineering Team, reporting to the Head of Engineering and collaborating closely with the Chief Innovation Officer to ship features that make a real difference for students and educators.You’ll be joining a small and growing team of talented software engineers working together to solve the problems teachers and students face every day. We’re building a world where every student can succeed, and we need you to help us make that happen.You will:Architect the video generation pipeline end to end. Design the gen-AI pipeline that transforms lesson specifications into storyboards, scene graphs, scripts, and production plans. Every stage emits deterministic lessons-as-code and structured intermediate artifacts — scene specs, asset manifests, timing maps — that can be inspected, versioned, cached, diffed, and selectively re-rendered. Ship multiple substantial features per week. This is a minimum velocity bar, not an exaggeration. You will leverage AI and agentic coding to build incredible software, very, very quickly. Build the multi-agent production workflow. Develop agentic orchestration (LangGraph or equivalent) in which an orchestrator delegates to specialist agents: pedagogy analyst, instructional scriptwriter, slide designer, animator, narrator, and a panel of graders, evaluators, and LLM judges, with structured outputs and human-in-the-loop labeling and fine-tuning. Engineer the video generation pipeline. Build brand-consistent, design-system-driven video generation from structured content: layout engines and templates, LaTeX/KaTeX mathematical typesetting, programmatic diagrams and charts, and text-faithful image generation for illustrations with automated readability checks. Design programmatic motion to support worked examples with narration: kinetic typography, transitions, animated number lines and area models. Run parallelized rendering with generative video models (e.g. Veo / Kling / Seedance). Narration with TTS (e.g. ElevenLabs v3 / Gemini-TTS) audio tags and SSML, pronunciation lexicons for mathematical vocabulary, consistent voice identities across a course, multi-voice dialogue, multilingual narration, and open license music embeds. Build the ground-truth quality system. Construct golden datasets of spec-to-video pairs annotated by educators. Implement rubric-based scoring with calibrated LLM- and VLM-as-judge evaluators: frame-level visual fidelity, verification of on-screen mathematics, A/V sync validation, pedagogical fidelity checks against the source spec's learning objectives, reading-level analysis, and K-12 content safety screens.
