title: Chief of Staff, Emergency Cash (Senior Manager)
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! Location: Remote. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment Visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time. About this role GiveDirectly is scaling our emergency response operations to reach more people, faster, with cash after a crisis. Our belief is that cash assistance, delivered quickly after a crisis, is more effective and dignified than in kind assistance for most populations in crisis. As the portfolio grows, so does the need for strong operating systems, clear strategic priorities, and compelling positioning that helps EC build trust and influence across the humanitarian ecosystem. As Senior Manager, Emergency Cash Chief of Staff you will serve as a strategic partner to EC leadership, helping the team operate more effectively and increase its impact. You will own performance management systems, strategic planning processes, and key operating mechanisms that ensure visibility into priorities, progress, and outcomes. You will also lead strategic initiatives that strengthen how Emergency Cash is positioned internally and externally, including advancing GiveDirectly's "Brand as Access" strategy to build recipient trust and deepen engagement with key stakeholders. This role sits at the intersection of strategy, operations, and organizational effectiveness. You will work across teams to improve decision-making, create scalable systems and resources, develop core EC messaging and collateral, and support high-priority strategic initiatives. The ideal candidate is a structured problem solver who enjoys turning ambiguity into action, building systems that help teams perform at a high level, and driving cross-functional work from concept through execution. Reports to: Senior Product Director, Emergency Cash Level: Senior Manager EC Chief of Staff Travel Requirement: Must be able to travel up to 40% of the time including ~1-2 times per year for team retreats. What you'll do Performance Management & Organizational Effectiveness Own EC goal performance monitoring systems, dashboards, and review processes to ensure visibility into key metrics, priorities, and outcomes. Drive strategic planning and goal-setting processes, helping the team align around clear objectives and measurable results. Improve operating rhythms, meeting structures, and decision-making processes to maximize team effectiveness. Develop and maintain evergreen systems, playbooks, and operating resources that increase institutional knowledge and execution quality. Brand as Access Develop and advance an EC ‘Brand as Access strategy,’ positioning GD’s Emergency Cash public profile to ensure recipient trust and unlock relationships with mobile network operators, financial service providers, governments and other stakeholders. Partner across GiveDirectly to ensure EC messaging for access is consistent, compelling, aligned across external-facing channels and integrated and aligned with our fundraising and systems change messaging. Own the creation and maintenance of core EC collateral, including pitch decks, webpages, FAQs, briefing materials, one-pagers, and strategic narratives. MNO Relationship Management Support the management of GiveDirectly’s strategic Mobile Network Operator (MNO) partnerships by coordinating engagement plans, tracking commitments, and ensuring timely follow-up on key actions across partners and internal teams. Develop and maintain the systems, trackers, and reporting needed to provide visibility into partnership status, key milestones, risks, and opportunities. Special Projects Lead high-priority strategic initiatives that advance Emergency Cash objectives and team effectiveness. Serve as a strategic thought partner to EC leadership on emerging opportunities, risks, and long-term priorities. Collaborate with the fundraising team on addressable market analysis, market segmentation, and framing of EC products Qualifications Required Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly's values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. 6+ years of experience in strategy, operations, management consulting, business operations, organizational effectiveness, product strategy, or a related field in a mission-driven or high-performance environment. Demonstrated experience building systems, processes, and operating mechanisms that improve team performance, accountability, and organizational effectiveness. Experience leading strategic planning, goal-setting, performance management, or business review processes. Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to identify patterns, synthesize insights, and translate findings into actionable recommendations. Excellent project management skills and a track record of independently driving complex, cross-functional initiatives from inception through execution. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, including experience creating executive-level presentations, strategic documents, and stakeholder-facing materials. Ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders without direct authority while balancing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Ability to thrive in ambiguity, proactively identify opportunities for improvement, and build practical solutions that scale with high ownership. Experience developing messaging, positioning, stakeholder engagement strategies, or go-to-market approaches for products, programs, or initiatives. Preferred Experience conducting market analysis, audience segmentation, landscape assessments, or strategic research to inform organizational decision-making. Experience creating executive communications, strategic collateral, presentations, or thought leadership materials. Familiarity with AI tools and workflows, including experience identifying opportunities to improve productivity, knowledge management, or decision-making through technology. Experience working in humanitarian response, international development, public sector, social impact, or adjacent sectors. Experience supporting senior leadership teams, chief-of-staff functions, or cross-functional strategic initiatives. Experience with data visualization, dashboarding, or performance management tools. Priority application deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Early applications are heavily encouraged. We’re growing at incredible speed, and expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. We’re hiring a Chief Technology Officer to lead the building and rebuilding of the technology, systems and ways of working that will enable a sustained $5B+ p/a operation. You will build software that safely and securely moves billions of dollars to millions of vulnerable people in some of the poorest and highest need parts of the world. This will require applying excellent engineering, team building and organizational judgment to complex, high-stakes operations: identity and fraud management, machine learning on large but imperfect datasets (cell phone data, satellite imagery, government registries), mobile money integrations, low-connectivity environments, rapidly evolving requirements all in diverse regulatory environments and country contexts. You’ll need to keep our legacy technology stack stable and performant, while in parallel building new systems from the ground up for our next level of scale. You will lead engineering, data, security and enterprise technology – with a small, mighty and rapidly growing engineering team of ~15, and the expectation that this can at least double to ~30 in the next 12 months if you want it to. You’ll report to a CEO with deep experience running technology companies, and partner with our VP Product. This role is remote, with working hours between US Eastern Time and East African Time, and some preference for candidates in our office hubs of New York, London, or Nairobi. What we’re looking for: An exceptional hirer, manager and organizer of technical talent. Proven record identifying, hiring, developing and retaining excellent engineers and engineering leaders, and creating team processes that consistently deliver software with quality and velocity. Deep technical judgment, applied close to the work. You can evaluate major designs, pressure-test architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, and recognize when a team is heading the wrong way, without becoming the primary implementer. Low-ego: you’ll investigate a problem yourself when that’s what the situation requires. Business judgment and decisiveness under ambiguity. You’re not just a technical leader, you’re also a business executive. You understand the business, are a strong cross-functional partner, and have a history of good judgment when navigating tradeoffs of long vs. short term, speed, reliability, security, flexibility, cost, technical quality, and user impact. AI first. You have a point of view on where AI meaningfully changes engineering productivity and organizational capability, and you’ve moved a team from experimentation to real, measured use. You can set the tools, culture, goals, and guardrails that leverage the opportunities and mitigate the risks of an AI first engineering culture. Embody and set an example for GD values. We take our values incredibly seriously, and expect our leaders to embody, nurture, and promote them in the way they work and the teams they build. Advantages, not requirements. Experience in an operationally complex or regulated domain (fintech, payments, humanitarian response, global development); systems involving financial controls, fraud risk, identity, or sensitive recipient data; operating across multiple countries, particularly lower-income or infrastructure-constrained ones; leading both modern product engineering and enterprise technology. What you’ll do Define our technology vision and target stack. Own the technical strategy for technology-first delivery at $5B+/year: architecture, platforms, build-vs-buy, and what we retire. Work with executive, product, finance, risk, and data leaders to turn program and product strategy into a sequenced, credible portfolio of technical investments. Balance a demanding portfolio. You'll manage six workstreams that all matter and won't all move at once: (1) building our new cash delivery stack (remote-first verification, fraud prevention, massive volume) (2) stabilizing our legacy stack until switchover, then managing the migration; (3) donor-facing fundraising products; (4) our global emergency cash system (and eventual white-labelling of that product); (5) enterprise technology; (6) internal tooling, platform, and cybersecurity. Deciding sequencing and staffing across these (and saying "not yet" credibly) is the job. Build and grow an exceptional technology organization. Recruit outstanding engineering and technology talent, design the org GiveDirectly needs at its next stage of scale (engineering, product, data, security, infrastructure, enterprise systems), and create the accountability, decision rights, and career paths to sustain high talent density. Grow the engineering team from 15 to ~30 with a lean but durable management structure. Own the technical direction and quality bar. Guide consequential decisions on integrations, data, security, reliability, and technical debt. Ensure our systems can safely support a major increase in transaction volume, geographic reach, and organizational dependence on technology. Set a pragmatic quality bar appropriate to high-stakes financial delivery while preserving speed. Lead across organizational boundaries. Serve as a member of GiveDirectly’s executive team, reporting to the CEO and bringing technology into major strategic and operating decisions. Help non-technical leaders understand technical constraints and costs, build credibility with country and functional leaders by understanding their realities, and force clarity when priorities, ownership, or tradeoffs are ambiguous. Travel. Approximately 4–6 trips per year, including visits to GiveDirectly countries of operation. Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. Location: This role must be based in Kampala. About GiveDirectly Uganda Since 2013, we've delivered over $94M directly to more than 120,000 people across more than 16 districts in Uganda, including long-term self-reliance programs for refugees, poverty relief projects in Karamoja and other districts, and anticipatory cash ahead of climate-related disasters. We've proven the model. Now we're ready to go much bigger. Over the next few years, our ambition for Uganda is to dramatically scale transfer volume—reaching thousands more recipients—while building the efficiency to do it sustainably. This isn't incremental growth. It's a step-change in what's possible, and we're hiring the person who will lead it. This person will also lead a talented team deeply committed to the communities they work in and to helping more households move out of poverty. The role The Country Director is the most senior GiveDirectly presence in Uganda, with full accountability for the country office: programs, operations, external relations, team, and strategy. Most of the job is delivery. You own whether transfers go out on time, at target cost, and at GD's quality bar, and whether that holds as volume grows. The rest of the job exists to protect and extend that: controls that keep money and recipients safe as the operation gets bigger, a team that can execute, partnerships that lower our cost or widen our reach, and a strategy that concentrates effort on what actually moves impact. What you'll own Program management Accountable for GD Uganda's programs running on time, at target efficiency, and at GD's quality standards: Own the delivery plan: Drive operational excellence across all Uganda programs through a comprehensive project management plan. Own the KPIs: Throughput, cost per recipient, payment success/error rates, recipient experience, and enrollment-to-payment cycle time. Fix problems at the root: Diagnose delivery issues structurally—redesign processes, staffing models, or systems rather than managing by escalation. Be a thought partner: Provide analytical support to help the team clear execution bottlenecks. Build for scale: Design the operation needed for the next order of magnitude, not just the one that exists today. Steward the budget: Manage country spend to maximize the ratio of donor funds converted into transfers. Manage risk: Identify, evaluate, and mitigate strategic and operational risks across programs. Risk, safeguarding, and integrity Delivering cash creates real risk, and it scales with volume. Every new district, partner, and payment channel is a new surface for fraud, exclusion error, and harm to recipients. We expect the Country Director to own that exposure personally, not to delegate it to a committee. Own fraud and safeguarding outcomes for the country office: design the prevention controls, monitor the leading indicators, and act on what they tell you before problems compound. Set a culture where staff and recipients report concerns and trust that something happens when they do, including accessible recipient feedback and grievance channels. Chair the country's internal audit, safeguarding, and program coordination forums, and partner closely with GD's global internal audit, compliance, finance, and safeguarding teams. Provide leadership and oversight of investigations into alleged misconduct, and handle disciplinary outcomes with zero tolerance for fraud or safeguarding violations. Ensure country compliance with global standards, and translate global policy into protocols that make sense in the Ugandan context. Team management Lead a large team across programs, field operations, finance, HR, procurement, internal audit, and safeguarding, directly managing the country management team. Build managers who can run their own functions: clear expectations, real feedback, visible growth paths. Lead workforce planning and succession, keeping the team lean as the operation grows. Set the tone on GD's values. Partnerships and government relations Own GD's relationship with the Government of Uganda, line ministries, district authorities, and the government-led social protection and relief programs we coordinate with. Secure and maintain the government permissions that programs depend on at the national and district levels. Build and deepen the commercial and delivery partnerships that improve impact per dollar: mobile network operators and payment providers, data and identity systems, and implementing or referral partners who extend our reach. Represent GiveDirectly publicly in Uganda, to government, media, and the sector. Steward existing donor relationships and host funder and partner visits to the field, working with GD's global fundraising team, which leads donor sourcing and proposal development. Shape ambitious program designs and budgets that global fundraising can take to funders. Strategic planning Lead vision-setting and strategic planning for the Uganda country office. Set country operational and revenue goals and create a roadmap for success. Make and defend hard deprioritization calls. Bring Uganda's perspective into GD's global strategy, policy, and cross-country planning. What you'll bring We're looking for an experienced operator who has led complex delivery at scale, knows the operation through its numbers, and has built the systems, teams, and controls it takes to grow. The core of what we're looking for: 5–10 years of experience in a similar role or function. People management experience (experience hiring and building a team preferred). Strong relationship management, including hands-on experience engaging government at national or district level, not necessarily as the principal. Exceptional communication skills: speaking, writing, presenting, and negotiating, especially with senior audiences and funders. Outstanding project management skills. Analytical problem solver: you approach problems with an analytical, iterative mindset and a strong prioritization framework. You can run robust analyses to inform management and programming decisions. Enthusiasm for fast-paced environments, which may lack a predefined playbook for success and involve significant “learning by doing.” Experience in partnerships and business development. Strong alignment with GD values. Strongly desired Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa and fluency in the operating context. About this Role We are currently planning for a significant increase in scale, and we are building the People function that can carry it. This is a new role with two halves. First half: you will be the dedicated people partner to our Global Shared Services (GSS) teams [~200 employees], who do not have one today, working primarily with people leaders on structure, workforce planning, talent, and the people decisions that come with growth. You will partner with and coach senior leaders across GSS, up to VP level, including those who are strong operators still growing as people leaders. Second half: you will build how we handle behavior and performance concerns across the organization: the standards, the decision framework, and the enablement that lets people managers and our HR teams in the field handle them well. The first year is weighted toward that build, with partnering also focused on performance and talent management as the most pressing needs. As the standards land, the balance shifts toward deeper partnering, while you continue to own the employee relations model. The reason for this weight: the employee relations build is our most acute gap today, but should not be construed as a ceiling of the job. Over time, the partnering half opens up well beyond performance and conduct into org design, workforce planning, talent, career development, and the full range of people strategy for our global functions. We're hiring a broad, senior people partner who can build the ER model as their first major deliverable, not an employee relations specialist. If your instinct on reading this is that the ER work is the whole job, this role probably isn't the right fit, and the reverse is also true: if you're only interested in the strategic partnering and not the build, year one will frustrate you. Job type: Full-time Reports to: Head of People Level: Director Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time. Travel: Approximately 3-4 trips per year, including at least one to a country of operation and one to a key in-person leadership moment, with occasional additional travel as sensitive or time-critical situations require. Lead org design and workforce planning for global functions as we scale: structure, role definition, levels, sizing and sequencing, in partnership with function leads, Finance and Talent Acquisition. Own talent and succession for the population: who is ready for more, who is a flight risk, and where the single points of failure sit. Partner on performance and compensation decisions for global staff, including calibration, promotion cases and band placement. Coach senior leaders, on their own leadership as much as on their teams. Lead people-side change for global functions: restructures, leadership transitions, and the team-level fallout of both. Act as the People representative for global staff, holding employment decisions within our framework in the way HR Managers do in their countries. Coach global managers through behavior and performance conversations, rather than taking those conversations from them. Build how we handle behavior and underperformance: Define what these categories actually are and communicate them across the organization, so that a concern can be routed rather than defaulting into a disciplinary process. Audit how each country handles cases end to end, and write one global standard per category covering intake, escalation, who is responsible at each stage, and documentation. Build from what already works and flex only where local law genuinely requires it. Build the employment decision framework with Legal, including a delegated authority matrix setting out who decides what and when, and the escalation route when a case falls outside it. Design and deliver enablement for the three groups who have to use all of this: managers, HR Managers, and staff. Work with our central investigations function to stand up a single record of outcomes, so that patterns and inconsistencies become visible. Within your first 90 days, recommend who should support behavior and underperformance cases in each country, and what that requires. Hold consistency across the organization: Coach HR Managers through cases in their countries, and act as the technical escalation point when they need one. Watch outcomes as they accumulate, and raise it when something looks inconsistent: comparable facts resolving differently, one country diverging, or a pattern clustering around a team or a manager. What this role is not: Not an investigations role. Misconduct investigations sit with our Central Intake and Investigations Hub. You define what managers need to know about employee relations; they own the curriculum and the channel. Who we're looking for: Required: 7+ years of HR business partner experience with executive and senior leaders, including coaching leaders who were strong in their domain but needed to grow as people leaders, and holding a position when it was unpopular. Demonstrated experience building employee relations standards, policy or frameworks from scratch or close to it, and getting them adopted across multiple countries or business units. A mix of high-growth commercial or tech experience and international or mission-driven experience. The role needs the speed and build instinct of the first and the operating complexity of the second, and we think it is hard to do well with only one. Experience holding or closely advising on disciplinary and capability decisions, including dismissals, in more than one jurisdiction, with the judgment to know when to bring in counsel. A track record of influencing without formal authority in a matrixed organization. Judgment and steadiness. You can hold a position with a senior leader, be wrong in public when you are, and stay trusted either way. Preferred: Experience operating in sub-Saharan Africa. The Program Manager (PM) will work with the Internal Audit Director and the wider Internal Audit team to design innovations to manage the risks associated with cash transfers. Reports to: Director, Internal Audit Level: Manager Location: Remote - Goma/Bukavu/Kinshasa, DRC with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours. Role Summary Supports overall Global Internal Audit (IA) strategy. Overall risk manager for the countries in their portfolio. In partnership with the Country Director (CD), lead the development of the country IA strategy. Supports on all project design at all stages (project inception, proposal creation, project design, risk register creation, ongoing project risk management, project closure). Leads (or where relevant, delegates) all country syncs with CD. HR oversight (not direct management) for all countries in their portfolio. Takes direct lead on certain, more sensitive and high risk investigations in portfolio (as determined by CD and IAD). Manages Internal Audit for each country in their portfolio Manages Internal Audit Manager (IAM) directly. Supports admin oversight and procurement for the IA team in country (ensuring docs are in order etc). Carries out regular spot checks on country operations and ensures IAM is doing their checks and documenting them. Leads coordination with other internal teams (such as Safeguarding, Programs, and Tech) as well as external partners, such as Telcos where needed. Visits each country in portfolio at least 1x per year for field visits. Roles and responsibilities: Project Design (25%) Represent IA in country project design conversations, including development of strategic risk management measures. Owning development of project-specific Internal Audit proposals detailing audit rates, audit approaches, e.t.c. for new projects and discussing these with CD. Oversee community risk scoping exercises and ensure full scoping report is submitted to IAD and CDs for all new projects. Ensure that customized risk registers are created for all new projects; ensure that risk registers for ongoing projects are updated regularly. Review implementation tools, e.g. enrollment surveys, to better align them to risk detection, mitigation and prevention. Systems Orientated risk monitoring (45%) Owning and monitoring IA metrics / KPIs in countries of portfolio and owning correction of dropping or critically missed metrics. Overall owner (accountable) of country project workbooks detailing workplans and staffing, tech related requirements and activity timelines. Define and review risk classifications based on projects and country level activities. Hold weekly (or bi-weekly) meetings with Country Directors in each country you are assigned. Lead the development of escalation protocols for different types of risks and monitor implementation of the protocols by country managers. Lead the transparent, accountable and where needed collaborative investigation of high risk cases. Support the IAM to undertake community based fraud intelligence monitoring exercises and escalate any identified risk trends to the CD and IAD. Monitor the traffic and trends of risk reporting and flag high risk countries and projects to the CD and IAD. Support the IAD with tech-related fraud prevention innovations work through different inputs as may be requested from time to time. Where relevant, build in-country relationships with fraud management stakeholders (for example, MoMo provider telcos) for sustainable fraud resolutions in-country. Conduct spot checks on both the programs and IA operations to ensure high quality and identify any abnormalities. Build and manage in-country project related stakeholder relationships; working with different in-country teams to ensure IA deliverables are tracked as per workplan. Write and share with the IA - Director, quarterly productivity reports and/or project specific retrospectives (or progress reports). People Management (10%) Directly manages Internal Audit Managers in all countries you are assigned. Conduct regular check-ins with Direct Reports. Conduct performance reviews for direct reports every quarter and provide a report of the same to the IA-Director and CD where relevant. Indirectly support the AFMs and FOs in the countries you are assigned. Develop a team with a high capacity for problem solving, critical thinking, and strong analytical and communication skill. Conduct regular skip-level meetings with AFMs. Hiring: Directly responsible for hiring IAMs in the countries you are assigned. Create a strong overall team Manage conflicts and other risks within the team and escalate where appropriate. Promote effective team culture by encouraging recognition of positive achievements and other team-building initiatives. Model ethical behavior that encourages the team to report misconduct within GD staff, partners, community and recipients. Conduct staff career growth needs assessments (through structures surveys and 1:1 sessions) and liaise with the HR manager to deliver robust professional development sessions internally and externally. Culture Building (10%) Act as the custodian of ‘Recipients First’ Value within the team by ensuring compliance to policies and protocols of GiveDirectly. Maintain an active, visible and consistent commitment to a common standard of behavior that is required throughout every aspect of the organization as stipulated in the Code of Conduct Statement. Manage a team that is driven by individual accountability involving moving beyond corporate ‘rules-based’ behavior to ‘values-based’ behavior that promotes a greater focus on promoting individual integrity.” Identify sub-cultures within the organization that may result in safeguarding and fraud risks to recipients. Conduct annual training to country Programs teams on fraud and safeguarding mitigation requirements as outlined in GD policies. Other responsibilities (10%) Supports Director on reflecting on and rethinking the Global IA strategy and mandate. Supports Director on utilizing AI and technology to improve GD’s fraud risk management systems. Participates in weekly IA management meetings and weekly sprints to discuss cross-team activities. Support on country external audits where requested. Support on non-field based fraud management on an as-needed basis in your countries of operation. Proactively identify and flag ways to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of IA’s operations. Support other country of operations outside of portfolio where necessary. What you’ll bring: Internal audit / risk management background - 3+ years leading audit, compliance, or risk functions, ideally in a role that combined strategy design with hands-on fieldwork (not just desk audits). Fraud investigation experience - has personally led or overseen sensitive/high-risk investigations, not just routine checks. People management - directly managed a team, including hiring, performance reviews, and conflict management. Cross-country or multi-site portfolio experience - managed risk/audit across several countries or regional units simultaneously, since this role owns a country portfolio. Field-based operations exposure - comfortable with in-person field visits (at least 1x/year per country) in low-resource or humanitarian/development settings, not purely office-based audit work. Stakeholder management - experience liaising with external partners and internal cross-functional teams (Safeguarding, Programs, Tech). Data/analytics fluency - experience using data to detect fraud trends, build KPIs/metrics, and monitor risk reporting, plus openness to AI/tech-driven fraud prevention tools. Program/project design experience - has contributed to project design, risk registers, and proposal creation, ideally in an NGO, cash-transfer, or development-sector context. Report writing at a senior level - track record producing strategy documents, quarterly reports, and retrospectives for leadership. Fluency in both English and French. Alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. About GiveDirectly in the DRC GiveDirectly DRC was established in 2018 to enable cash transfers to poor and rural populations via mobile phones, thereby promoting food security, poverty reduction, and financial inclusion. We aimed to demonstrate the operational feasibility and cost-effectiveness of transferring large volumes of money digitally in one of the world's least developed countries. Since its inception four years ago, GiveDirectly DRC has used mobile phones to transfer over $14 million to more than 65,000 beneficiaries in four provinces: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, and Kinshasa. GiveDirectly's activities in the DRC have expanded to include, among other things: compelling proofs of concept for mobile-based cash transfers; and the implementation of innovative technologies to target disadvantaged urban populations in Kinshasa, in collaboration with the DRC's social protection agency, the DRC Social Fund. The delivery of contactless cash to beneficiaries in Beni and Bunia affected by the economic consequences of COVID-19. You will be joining Give Directly DRC at an exciting time in its history, as we are establishing and hope to launch several new programs and strengthen our partnership with the DRC government. About the Role As Senior Manager, Operations (DRC), you'll build and lead the operational backbone behind GiveDirectly's programs in the country. You'll direct the support services team end-to-end — HR, logistics, procurement, and administration — while managing a team of managers. You'll design a procurement strategy that keeps goods and services flowing efficiently and reliably across provinces, own fleet and logistics management as the program scales, and manage the operational budget with an eye for efficiency. You'll also support the Country Director on HR strategy — recruitment, training, and performance — and design the systems needed for a much larger footprint across provinces, from procurement to digital tools that improve scalability. This is a role for someone who can build systems as readily as they can lead people, and who's energized by both strategic design and the operational details that make it real on the ground. What You’ll Do: Lead the DRC support services team end-to-end — HR, logistics, procurement, administration, and office management — including direct oversight of managers Develop and drive a procurement strategy ensuring efficient, compliant, and resilient sourcing across provinces, and own fleet and logistics management as the program scales Manage the operational budget, forecasting and driving efficiency across procurement, logistics, and administrative spend Support the Country Director on HR strategy — recruitment, training, performance management, and talent density — through oversight of the HR function Design systems and processes to support a much larger footprint across provinces, anticipating future needs and identifying AI and digital opportunities to improve scalability Coach and develop support services managers to build operational excellence beyond individual contribution Maintain a compliance and operational risk register, and lead internal spot checks, audit preparedness, and action plans in partnership with Finance and Internal Audit Own donor reporting, budget tracking, and donor visit coordination, and serve as the primary point of contact between the Country Office and GSS on operational and compliance matters Own the Operational Knowledge Base and lead onboarding, training, and localization of materials as the team grows Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (management, administration, finance, or related); a master's degree is an asset Minimum 6 years of experience in operations management, with a track record of transforming informal systems into structured, compliant, and scalable ones, including direct oversight of managers Strong financial and budget management skills, with experience managing an operational budget Proven experience maintaining a risk register and working closely with internal/external audit functions Experience developing and coaching managers, with comfort delegating execution while retaining accountability for results Strong digital fluency, with experience using and training teams on multiple platforms (Google Suite, Salesforce, Asana, Guru, Slack) Familiarity with international NGO standards and donor compliance frameworks Experience navigating the DRC's complex legal environment, including labor law and immigration requirements Strong alignment with GiveDirectly's values Excellent written and oral communication skills, including ability to communicate fluently in English and French with high level stakeholders Professional proficiency in French and English required; title: Director of Delivery Operations
descriptionText: Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions. Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most. With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact. At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts. Code for America is looking for a talented Director of Delivery Operations who will establish and embed the delivery practices, standards, and governance mechanisms that build on existing best practices while enabling our teams to execute with consistency and confidence across a growing portfolio of government-facing projects — from kick-off through to successful project completion. About the role: Code for America works across a portfolio of complex, high-stakes projects — from products to technology-enabled advisory services — all aimed at helping millions of people access critical government benefits and services. As our portfolio grows and the demands on our government partners intensify, the consistency and discipline of how we deliver matters as much as what we deliver. The Director of Delivery Operations will build and steward the systems, standards, and practices that make our project delivery excellent and repeatable. This is an internal-facing, enabling role: you won't manage individual projects directly, but you'll shape how every Safety Net advisory project runs — from the moment a partnership is handed off from cultivation through to project close. You'll work closely with Program Directors, Project Sponsors, and key project and discipline leaders to embed practical delivery practices into day-to-day work, and you'll partner with senior program leadership to ensure our operating model stays grounded in what actually works in the field. This is a new role at Code for America, and the person who takes it on will have real strategic ownership — setting the priorities for how we invest in delivery infrastructure, making deliberate tradeoffs about where to standardize versus where to leave room for project-specific judgment, and bringing the best of delivery practice, AI-enabled tools and capabilities, and human-centered approaches to improving government services to keep Code for America at the leading edge of how this work gets done. This role will report to the Senior Director of Safety Net and is expected to travel no more than 15% of the time. Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position. In this position you will: Delivery Standards & Practice Ownership Own and continuously improve Code for America's delivery methodology, including project management standards, tools, templates, playbooks, and governance frameworks Set and drive strategic priorities for delivery infrastructure investment in alignment with senior leaders — uplifting explicit tradeoffs about where standardization adds the most value and where over-prescribing would create friction rather than consistency ⁠— while bringing leaders and project teams along. Design and maintain protocols for the full project lifecycle: information handoffs from the Partnerships team at cultivation close, project kickoff facilitation and team onboarding, scope revision processes, and project close-out. Collaborate with product operations to leverage learnings and best practices for common processes across product and advisory work. Own and administer delivery tooling (e.g., Asana, Airtable), including how it's configured, how projects are structured within it, and how it supports visibility into project effectiveness across the portfolio Maintain a living library of easy-to-use delivery resources — templates, how-to guides, playbooks — that teams can access and apply without reinventing the wheel Identify and integrate AI tools into delivery workflows where they can meaningfully improve consistency, efficiency, or quality of execution, modeling responsible adoption for the broader team Coaching, Adoption & Change Management Note: The Director of Delivery Operations role is a people management role, but it is not expected to have direct reports initially. This role may eventually support in growing out a team, adopting direct reports as management needs evolve. Provide day-to-day support to project leaders to ensure delivery standards are understood and consistently applied across their projects Roll out training, tools & resources, and onboarding support to build project management capability across program teams Drive adoption of delivery standards through intentional change management — not just defining the practices, but creating the conditions for people to use them consistently Anticipate any resistance to new delivery practices before it surfaces, and work to understand and address it proactively, rather than waiting for adoption to stall Design and facilitate feedback loops — through quality assurance reviews, retrospectives, and structured check-ins — that surface what's working and what needs to evolve Identify patterns across projects (recurring risks, scope issues, handoff breakdowns) and translate them into updated guidance and coaching Project Support & Scope Management Ensure strong communication and feedback loops with project teams to track delivery effectiveness, surface emerging risks, and provide hands-on support when projects need to course-correct from a project management perspective. Support scope revision processes from a project management perspective, helping teams manage and reset expectations in a structured way — partnering closely with leaders across disciplines throughout. Partner with the Partnerships team to ensure smooth handoffs at the transition from cultivation to delivery, with clear shared accountability and no loss of critical context. Governance & Portfolio Visibility Continually assess effectiveness and efficiency of existing and new governance mechanisms, including regular project check-ins, reporting, and communication processes that give senior leadership timely visibility into project status, risks, and delivery effectiveness across the portfolio. Recommend and implement changes to improve them. Track adoption of delivery standards across projects and flag gaps proactively Support Program Directors in preparing for project reviews and escalations with consistent, well-structured information Partner with senior program leadership to ensure delivery operations stay aligned with evolving program priorities and organizational strategy Anticipate systemic challenges across the portfolio before they become blockers, and develop solutions that address root causes rather than individual project symptoms Other duties as assigned Engage in ad hoc projects and initiatives as required by the organization's evolving needs. About you: This position is a great fit for an experienced delivery professional who thrives in an enabling and coaching role — someone who gets energy from building systems that help others succeed, who knows the importance of defining a standard, and who has the strategic instincts to set priorities, make tradeoffs, and bring people along through change. 8+ years of experience in project management, delivery operations, or a PMO function, ideally within a digital services, consulting, government, or related civic technology organization Demonstrated experience designing and implementing delivery frameworks, standards, or playbooks Demonstrated ability to set priorities across a delivery domain — deciding where to invest in standardization, where to leave flexibility, and how to communicate those tradeoffs to senior stakeholders Strong coaching and change management skills, with a track record of driving adoption of new practices across teams and anticipating resistance before it becomes a blocker Ability to learn fast, act with conviction, and stay open to feedback — you don't need perfect information to move, and are open to making adjustments as you learn more. Experience facilitating project kickoffs and structuring handoff processes between teams or functions Deep familiarity with project and delivery management tools (e.g., Asana, Airtable, Jira, Smartsheet) and the ability to configure and support broad adoption Experience identifying and integrating AI tools into delivery or project management workflows, with a practical and responsible approach to doing so Experience supporting a portfolio of concurrent projects, with the ability to spot systemic delivery risks and support course-correction across programs Comfort working in a highly collaborative, cross-functional environment where influence matters more than authority — particularly in close partnership with product, partnerships, and program functions Experience navigating scope changes, escalations, and shifting partner expectations in complex, multi-stakeholder projects Curiosity about emerging AI tools and a commitment to using them responsibly and effectively A deep commitment to Code for America's mission of making government services work well for the people who need them most It’s a bonus if you have: Experience working in civic tech, government services, or public sector delivery contexts Familiarity with human-centered design or agile delivery methodologies as practiced in digital government work Experience building delivery operations functions from scratch in a growing or scaling organization Background working with or alongside government partners (state agencies, federal programs) Experience developing training curricula or facilitating communities of practice around delivery or project management What you’ll get - Salary: Code for America’s salary bands are transparent as a part of our commitment to transparency and fairness. As part of our hiring practices, we aim to target the midpoint of the 2nd quartile of the range for all new hires. Offer targets vary based on market / geographic location. At the core of this role is the belief that government services can and should work better for the people who depend on them most — and that achieving that requires sustained, expert leadership over complex, multi-stakeholder programs. title: Associate Data Engineer (Georgia Tech Only)
descriptionText: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We’re hiring Data Engineers graduating between December 2026 and June 2027 to join our data team in Miami, starting May or June 2027. This is not a rotational program and it isn’t a shadowing role. You’ll work on the pipelines and integrations that make OneImaging’s data the source of truth for the business - from the raw feed coming out of a payer, a provider, or our own platform, through the transformation logic, to the dashboard or automation that someone in operations, finance, or care navigation actually relies on every day. It also means you’ll be building alongside a team that has moved unusually early on AI-assisted engineering. We run a shared AI harness that every engineer’s agent builds on, and we’re explicit internally that writing code is no longer the slow part of the job - the slow parts are deciding what to build and verifying what comes out. We’ll expect you to use these tools heavily and to own everything they produce for you. What you'll do: Build and maintain data pipelines in Databricks (SparkSQL/PySpark) that ingest, transform, and validate data from sources like our platform databases, payer eligibility files, provider and claims systems, and third-party APIs - with a senior engineer as your mentor and reviewer Work across the full path a dataset takes - ingestion, transformation, modeling, and the Looker dashboard or downstream workflow it feeds - with guidance at first and increasing independence as you go Help build and maintain automated inbound/outbound file exchanges (eligibility, claims status, reporting) that other teams depend on to run their day-to-day operations Work with AI coding agents as a normal part of your workflow, and take full accountability for the output: you should be able to explain every file in your diff Write tests and validation checks for your pipelines, and treat data quality as part of shipping rather than a phase afterwards Participate in design reviews and code reviews from your first weeks - including reviewing other engineers’ work, because a bare approval with no comment isn’t a completed review here Ask why. We reason from first principles and we have an explicit norm that engineers are not implementation machines - if a requirement doesn’t make sense, we want you to say so Handle protected health information correctly, with data governance, access controls, and audit logging as first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts About you: Graduating with a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline between December 2026 and June 2027 You’ve built things nobody assigned you - side projects, coursework you took further than required, hackathon work, something with real data, however small Strong SQL skills and working knowledge of Python for data processing Some exposure to Databricks, Spark, or a similar distributed data processing tool - coursework, an internship, or a personal project is enough; we don’t expect production experience A basic mental model of how data moves from a source system into a warehouse or lakehouse and out to a report You use AI coding tools and you’ve formed opinions about them - including where they mislead you and how you catch it You can explain a technical decision you made and what you’d do differently, which matters more to us than the sophistication of the project Comfortable with ambiguity and with being told “we haven’t figured that out yet” Intellectually honest: you can change your mind when the evidence changes, and you’d rather delete your own work than defend it Clear written and verbal communication - you’ll be writing documentation and PR descriptions that other teams depend on Authorized to work in the United States, and able to be based in Miami Nice to have, and genuinely not required: An internship or co-op where you shipped a data pipeline or report to production Experience with a BI tool (Looker, Tableau, Power BI) or building a dashboard someone other than you used Exposure to AWS or another cloud provider Familiarity with relational or document databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB) Anything you’ve built on top of LLM or agent APIs - tools, harnesses, evals, agents Curiosity about healthcare data standards (HL7, FHIR, DICOM) or claims/eligibility data - we’ll teach you these, and we’d rather you question how things are done in healthcare than arrive already knowing Coursework or projects involving statistics, data modeling, or data warehousing concepts What we'll give you A published career framework with written promotion criteria, so you can see the path from Associate Software Engineer through Senior, Staff and Principal, and know exactly what's expected at each step. A mentor from among our senior engineers, for whom mentorship is a written part of their job. Real ownership, quickly. And a mission that's easy to get behind with real life impact. The base salary range for this position is $85,000 - $115,000. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans. Fraud and Security Notice: Please be aware of recent job scam attempts. Our team uses the oneimaging.com email domain exclusively. If you have been contacted by someone claiming to be a OneImaging recruiter or a hiring manager from a different domain about a potential job, please report it to law enforcement here and to candidateprotection@oneimaging.com. Equal Employment Opportunity: OneImaging is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and values diversity in the workplace. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. OneImaging is committed to providing accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at talent@oneimaging.com.

title: Full Stack Associate Software Engineer (Georgia Tech Only)
descriptionText: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We're hiring Full Stack Software Engineers graduating between December 2026 and June 2027 to join our engineering team in Miami, starting May or June 2027. This is not a rotational program and it isn't a shadowing role. You'll join one of our product squads and work across the whole stack — from the data model through the API to the interface a patient or a care navigator actually uses. Our engineering team is around twenty people, which means the work you ship is visibly yours and the distance between your code and a patient getting a scan scheduled is very short. It also means you'll be building alongside a team that has moved unusually early on AI-assisted engineering. We run a shared AI harness that every engineer's agent builds on, we have AI agents running in production behind guardrails and eval suites, and we're explicit internally that writing code is no longer the slow part of the job — the slow parts are deciding what to build and verifying what comes out. We'll expect you to use these tools heavily and to own everything they produce for you. What you'll do: Build and ship full stack features across our React frontend and TypeScript/Node.js backend, with a senior engineer as your mentor and reviewer Work across every layer of a feature — the migration, the API, the interface, the tests — with guidance at first and increasing independence as you go. Owning whole features end to end is the next step up our ladder, and it's a short step from here Work with AI coding agents as a normal part of your workflow, and take full accountability for the output: you should be able to explain every file in your diff Write tests across the stack, and treat verification as part of shipping rather than a phase afterwards Participate in design reviews and code reviews from your first weeks — including reviewing other engineers' work, because a bare approval with no comment isn't a completed review here Ask why. We reason from first principles and we have an explicit norm that engineers are not implementation machines — if a requirement doesn't make sense, we want you to say so Build features that handle protected health information correctly, with authentication, authorization, and audit logging as first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts About you: Graduating with a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline between December 2026 and June 2027 You've built things nobody assigned you — side projects, hackathon work, open-source contributions, something with real users, however few Working knowledge of JavaScript or TypeScript, and comfort with either React or Node.js. We care much more about how you reason than about which technologies you've already used Familiarity with relational databases and SQL, and a basic mental model of how a web request becomes a database query You use AI coding tools and you've formed opinions about them — including where they mislead you and how you catch it You can explain a technical decision you made and what you'd do differently, which matters more to us than the sophistication of the project Comfortable with ambiguity and with being told "we haven't figured that out yet" Intellectually honest: you can change your mind when the evidence changes, and you'd rather delete your own work than defend it Clear written and verbal communication — you'll be writing design docs and PR descriptions that other people depend on Authorized to work in the United States, and able to be based in Miami Nice to have, and genuinely not required: An internship or co-op where you shipped to production Experience with PostgreSQL, Express, or a typed API layer Anything you've built on top of LLM or agent APIs — tools, harnesses, evals, agents Testing experience with Jest, Vitest, Playwright, or similar Exposure to AWS or another cloud provider Curiosity about healthcare data standards (FHIR, HL7, DICOM) — we'll teach you these, and we'd rather you question how things are done in radiology than arrive already knowing A background in accessibility or internationalization What we'll give you A published career framework with written promotion criteria, so you can see the path from Associate Software Engineer through Senior, Staff and Principal, and know exactly what's expected at each step. A mentor from among our senior engineers, for whom mentorship is a written part of their job. Real ownership, quickly. And a mission that's easy to get behind with real life impact. You’re interested in why a company wins, how markets evolve, and how a brand can differentiate itself within a crowded or complex industry. - Comfort operating around senior leaders and subject matter experts. title: Staff Product Manager, Sourcing & Job Board
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Xometry is seeking a Staff Product Manager to own the strategy and lead the development of Sourcing and the Job Board: the systems that determine how manufacturing jobs are matched to partners so they win work that first their shop, succeed, and grow their business, while maximizing xometry’s sourcing margin. This is the commercial engine of the partner marketplace. Sourcing matches partner capability data to part and offer data and governs the priority and timing by which partners are shown available jobs. The Job Board is the surface where partners browse, evaluate and then accept/decline/bid/give feedback on the offers Xometry presents. The role sits at the intersection of partner performance, marketplace margin, and job quality, and it directly shapes how efficiently supply meets demand across a marketplace where thousands of partners take jobs every week. It is a senior individual-contributor position: the mandate is to own a major product domain end to end, set the technical product direction, and move the metrics that define marketplace health, chief among them sourcing margin, the number of partners actively taking jobs, and the quality of the matches partners receive. How You’ll Contribute: Own the multi-year strategic vision and roadmap for Sourcing and the Job Board, aligning matching and marketplace-liquidity strategy with Xometry's margin and growth objectives Drive the design and evolution of the matching and recommendation engine that pairs partner capabilities with the right jobs, along with the priority-scheduling logic that governs which partners see which offers, and when Own the job acceptance funnel end to end: grow the number of partners viewing the Job Board and raise the share who accept, spanning discovery, evaluation, and the accept, decline, and feedback loop that turns served offers into taken jobs Partner with the Pricing and Machine Learning teams to influence dynamic pricing and matching strategy. title: Salesforce Administrator
descriptionText: About TailorCare: TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a deeply personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By combining a careful assessment of patients’ symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose—and navigate—the most effective treatment pathway for them, every step of the way. TailorCare values the experiences and perspectives of individuals from all backgrounds. We are a highly collaborative, curious, and determined team passionate about scaling a high-growth start-up to improve the lives of those in pain. TailorCare is a remote-first company with a hybrid office in Nashville. About the Team: We are Team 2: Care Team Enablement, building solutions that enable our care team to serve more patients without working harder. Our solutions are primarily built on the Salesforce platform through our Seamline product, with additional services and integrations as needed. Our users are internal with two core roles: Care Advocates, who run outreach and get patients engaged, and Care Navigators, who handle clinical intakes and care coordination. Everything we ship lands in someone's daily work, so we stay close to the people using it. About the Role: We are looking for a Salesforce Administrator to join the team. Our instance is built on Health Cloud with Sales and Service Cloud capabilities behind our outreach, engagement, and care coordination workflows. We do not integrate directly with clinical care systems, but the org holds PHI under HIPAA, so access design and data handling matter here. You will work inside our sprints as a hands-on contributor rather than a ticket queue, carrying new features across the last mile and owning quality assurance for Salesforce releases. Key Responsibilities: Provision and maintain users, roles, profiles, permission sets, and licenses, and configure objects, fields, page layouts, and record types as new features land. Contribute to declarative automation alongside engineers, who continue to own automation where appropriate. Keep data clean: imports and exports, deduplication rules, and field-level data governance. Manage sandboxes and support releases from build through deployment. Build reports, dashboards, and the guardrails that let business teams self-serve where it makes sense. Write test plans, run manual regression on Salesforce releases, coordinate UAT sign-off, and keep the test case library and configuration docs current. Join sprint planning and design discussions, raise Salesforce-side risk early, and execute administrative business requests triaged and sized against a defined share of your capacity each sprint. Partner with Security and Compliance on least-privilege access design, access reviews, and PHI handling under HIPAA. Key Qualifications: 2-4 years administering a production Salesforce org. Strong command of the Salesforce sharing and security model, including org-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, and field-level security. Depth in Salesforce configuration (objects, fields, page layouts, record types) and hands-on Flow experience, including debugging flows you did not build. Working knowledge of SOQL, Salesforce reporting, and Data Loader or a comparable bulk data tool. Experience supporting a release process across sandboxes, and writing and executing manual test plans with UAT coordination. Demonstrated strong ownership of work coupled with an ability to collaborate openly and transparently. Health Cloud experience, or experience administering an org holding PHI under HIPAA or comparable regulated data, is preferred. Exposure to test automation practices, or the ability to read Apex and debug logs well enough to route an issue to an engineer, is preferred. Salesforce Administrator certification (ADM 201) is preferred, not required, and experience in healthcare and/or startups is a big plus. Pay Range $75,400—$92,400 USDWhat's In It For You Meaningful Work: We are dedicated to our mission and deeply value our patients and each other. Each day offers the opportunity to make a positive impact. Work Environment: We operate as a remote-first company with options for a hybrid work model in Nashville. Time Off: Our generous paid time off (PTO) and holiday plans ensure you have ample time to rest and recharge. Family First: We offer paid parental leave and support a healthy work-life balance, encouraging flexibility and autonomy. We love talking about our family and pets! Comprehensive Benefits: From Day 1, employees enjoy medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, wellness resources and an employer HSA contribution. Fair Compensation: We are committed to equitable pay for all team members and support your future goals with a 401k plan that includes employer matching. Community: We foster an inclusive environment where you can rely on your teammates, share honest feedback, and feel comfortable being your authentic self at work each day. TailorCare seeks to recruit and retain staff from diverse backgrounds and encourages qualified candidates to apply. TailorCare is an

title: Care Advocate (Shift: 8:00 am - 5:00 pm EST)
descriptionText: About TailorCare TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By carefully assessing patients' symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose and navigate the most effective treatment pathway for them every step of the way. TailorCare values the experiences and perspectives of individuals from all backgrounds. We are a highly collaborative, curious, and determined team passionate about scaling a high-growth start-up to improve the lives of those in pain. TailorCare is a remote-first company with our corporate office located in Nashville. About the Role As a Care Advocate, you will be responsible for engaging prospective patients through proactive outbound calls and multichannel outreach to drive awareness and enrollment in TailorCare’s musculoskeletal (MSK) care navigation program. You’ll often serve as the first point of contact, guiding patients through the value of our services and creating a personalized, empathetic, and compelling experience. This is a high-volume, outbound call center role focused on healthcare engagement, where you will connect with patients and their caregivers to identify barriers and motivate them to take action toward improved musculoskeletal (MSK) care. This is a non-exempt (hourly) position. Location & Schedule This is a 100% remote role. Candidates must be available to work hours aligned with Eastern, Central, or Mountain Time Zones. Responsibilities Conduct high-volume outbound calls and multichannel outreach (phone, SMS, email) to eligible patients to introduce TailorCare’s services and support program enrollment. Build and maintain a working knowledge of TailorCare’s MSK program, including core conditions, care pathways, eligibility criteria, and the enrollment process, to explain the program clearly and accurately. Clearly and empathetically communicate TailorCare’s value proposition, tailoring the conversation to patient goals, health literacy, concerns, and motivations. Build trust and rapport quickly using active listening, genuine empathy, and a compassionate approach that puts patients at ease and encourages engagement. Develop and apply foundational motivational interviewing (MI) techniques — including open-ended questioning, affirmations, reflective listening, and summarizing — to support patient-centered conversations. Identify and address common patient questions, barriers, or objections using established techniques while maintaining a calm, supportive tone; seek guidance and escalate appropriately when patient needs or situations fall outside your scope. Demonstrate empathy, professionalism, and consistency across all patient interactions, representing TailorCare’s values and mission. Document all patient interactions accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner within internal systems to support care coordination, data integrity, and reporting. Meet or exceed performance targets related to outreach volume, patient engagement, caseload management, and call quality. Use personal performance data and coaching feedback to identify trends in your own outreach and drive continuous self-improvement. Use AI-enabled tools and new technologies with curiosity, openness, and responsibility to improve personal productivity and outreach effectiveness. Adapt to changing scripts, tools, and workflows with a positive, growth-oriented mindset. Coordinate patient handoffs with internal care teams. Participate in regular team meetings and daily standups, contributing to a positive, inclusive culture of learning and collaboration. Surface observations, feedback, and ideas on patient trends, outreach barriers, or script effectiveness to appropriate team members for continuous improvement. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Required: Experience in outbound call center, inside sales, telephonic outreach, or patient engagement roles—preferably in a healthcare, health plan, or health tech environment. Strong written and verbal communication, persuasion, and active listening skills. Willingness to learn and apply motivational interviewing techniques in patient conversations. Ability to manage a high call volume while maintaining accuracy and empathy. Comfortable working with productivity targets and quality metrics in a fast-paced, tech-enabled environment. Ability to use personal performance data and feedback to drive self-improvement. High comfort level with technology, including contact center platforms, CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce), documentation tools, and Google Suite. Openness and adaptability to new technologies, including responsible use of AI-enabled tools. Ability to effectively collaborate with multidisciplinary teams. Excellent organizational and prioritization skills. Strong attention to detail. Ability and willingness to travel up to 10% as needed for onsite meetings, team collaboration, and company events. Preferred: Familiarity with motivational interviewing and/or patient coaching strategies. Experience working with Medicare populations and a basic understanding of Medicare Health Plans. Knowledge of medical terminology. Previous experience with remote/telemedicine care delivery. What's In It For You Meaningful Work: We are dedicated to our mission and deeply value our patients and each other. Each day offers the opportunity to make a positive impact. Work Environment: We operate as a remote-first company with options for a hybrid work model in Nashville. Time Off: Our generous paid time off (PTO) and holiday plans ensure you have ample time to rest and recharge. Family First: We offer paid parental leave and support a healthy work-life balance, encouraging flexibility and autonomy. We love talking about our family and pets! Comprehensive Benefits: From Day 1, employees enjoy medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, wellness resources and an employer HSA contribution. Fair Compensation: We are committed to equitable pay for all team members and support your future goals with a 401k plan that includes employer matching. Community: We foster an inclusive environment where you can rely on your teammates, share honest feedback, and feel comfortable being your authentic self at work each day. TailorCare seeks to recruit and retain staff from diverse backgrounds and encourages qualified candidates to apply. TailorCare is an
